Measured on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.9165, only modestly behind the larger DeBERTa NLI variants. It offers strong task-matched evidence while likely being more efficient.

It achieves the second-best measured result on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.9238. The model is explicitly an NLI cross-encoder, matching the entailment-focused structure of RobZamp/sick.

It has strong measured performance on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.9165. Although below the larger/base DeBERTa NLI models, it remains a robust task-matched option for SICK-style entailment classification.

Among the largest allowed general LLMs and one of the strongest 14B instruction-tuned models; fine-tuning or few-shot prompting on FiQA sentiment reliably yields top-tier results on short financial text.
Very strong 8B instruction model with excellent transfer to short-text sentiment; a proven, reliable baseline that fine-tunes cleanly on FiQA-scale data.
DeBERTa-v3-large is a top encoder for sentence-level sentiment/regression, and this NLI-tuned checkpoint already excels at zero/few-shot classification of short texts like FiQA headlines and posts.

A 13B model continued-pretrained on financial corpora, giving it domain vocabulary and context (earnings, tickers, market jargon) that boost sentiment accuracy on FiQA over generic LLMs of similar size.

Best-supported candidate because it appears in both sources and has strong biomedical token-classification evidence: PlanTL-GOB-ES/pharmaconer f1=0.9004 and PlanTL-GOB-ES/cantemist-ner f1=0.8334. Strong measured result on an English token-classification dataset similar in structure to ADE extraction: amirveyseh/acronym_identification f1=0.9199. Its span-marker formulation is a good fit for identifying entity spans such as drugs and adverse effects.

Has an excellent measured classification result on the retrieved neighborhood dataset DeepPavlov/clinc150 with accuracy=0.972. This supports the ADE classification configuration, though the evidence is less biomedical and does not directly cover token/relation extraction.

GNN-supported English model under the 14B limit with consistent measured results across multiple NLP benchmarks: allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.669, allenai/social_i_qa accuracy=0.669, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.669, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.669, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.669. Strongest task-language match among measured options: it achieved f1=0.9199 on amirveyseh/acronym_identification, an English expert-created token classification dataset similar to ADE’s span/entity extraction components.

Best biomedical/pharmacological-domain evidence: it achieved f1=0.9004 on PlanTL-GOB-ES/pharmaconer, a clinical NER dataset focused on pharmacological substances. The main limitation is that PharmaCoNER is Spanish while ade_corpus_v2 is English.

The GNN ranked it highest among the listed text models with combined score 0.0044, and it has consistent measured English task results including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.809, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.697, and allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.665. Its evidence is general rather than biomedical, but broad text understanding is strong.

A strong ≤14B English chat model with consistent measured results across several text benchmarks: allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.669, allenai/social_i_qa accuracy=0.669, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.669, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.669, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.669. It lacks biomedical-specific measurements but is a plausible general-purpose baseline.

It has a high measured QA result on CATIE-AQ/frenchQA with accuracy=0.7714 and f1=0.8874, and the GNN predicted-performance value is strong at 0.8091. However, the evidence is only one French QA dataset, so transfer to an English biomedical ADE corpus is uncertain.

RoBERTa continued-pretrained on biomedical papers (S2ORC); a well-established strong baseline for ADE and similar biomedical text classification/RE with excellent fine-tuning stability.

ModernBERT-large offers modern architecture (rotary, longer context, better efficiency) and strong general representations that fine-tune competitively for biomedical short-text classification.
Same DeBERTa-v3-large backbone with heavy NLI pretraining; a proven strong classification base that also enables zero/few-shot ADE-relevance prediction when labeled data is limited.

Best grounded candidate: it is consistently strong on two highly relevant English commonsense multiple-choice datasets, with allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.858 and HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA accuracy=0.857.

Strong measured commonsense performance on HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA with accuracy=0.834 supports fit for Cosmos QA. It also appears on allenai/quac with f1=0.449, giving some additional context-QA evidence though weaker than its CommonsenseQA result.

The GNN gives it the highest query score, combined=0.7322, and its measured QA track record is broad: allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.762, allenai/qasc accuracy=0.685, and allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.607. Although GNN support is weaker with combined=0.0282, its real measured reasoning and reading-comprehension results are strong: allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.9285 and EleutherAI/race accuracy=0.8287. These make it a plausible fit for contextual commonsense QA under the 14B-parameter constraint.

Best supported by consistent, highly relevant measured results: allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.858 and HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA accuracy=0.857. These are both English commonsense multiple-choice QA benchmarks close to Cosmos QA.

It has the strongest single measured result on the highly relevant allenai/openbookqa benchmark with accuracy=0.906. Evidence is from only one neighbor, but the benchmark’s commonsense reasoning focus makes it a strong candidate.

Shows strong English commonsense QA performance on HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA with accuracy=0.834, plus measured coverage on allenai/quac with f1=0.449. The CommonsenseQA result is especially relevant to Cosmos QA’s multiple-choice commonsense reasoning.

Performs well on the relevant allenai/openbookqa benchmark with accuracy=0.811. It lacks multi-dataset neighborhood evidence here, but the measured OpenBookQA result is strong for commonsense reasoning.

Has consistent measured results across two similar English QA datasets: allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.669 and allenai/quac accuracy=0.658. Scores are lower than the top models, but the cross-dataset evidence makes it a reliable fallback.

Strong measured QA and commonsense record: allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.9285, EleutherAI/race accuracy=0.8287, and allenai/hellaswag accuracy=0.8686. It also has EleutherAI/lambada_openai accuracy=0.8686 and truthful_qa_mc accuracy=0.5773, suggesting broad language understanding.

Excellent measured results on relevant reasoning and reading datasets, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.9285 and EleutherAI/race accuracy=0.8287. It also records EleutherAI/drop f1=0.5797 and Joschka/big_bench_hard accuracy=0.5018, giving stronger direct evidence than prediction alone.

Shows a reasonable measured record on several relevant benchmarks, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.7258, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.7111, and Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.5728. Largest allowed Qwen2.5 instruct model with SOTA-class commonsense/reading-comprehension scores among sub-15B models; well-suited to multiple-choice narrative QA like CosmosQA.
Newer 14B Qwen generation with even stronger reasoning; its native thinking mode further boosts multi-choice commonsense inference over passages.
R1-distilled reasoning on Qwen2.5-14B base yields excellent chain-of-thought for causal/commonsense MCQA, which matches CosmosQA's question style.
Gemma-2 9B instruct is one of the strongest sub-10B open models on HellaSwag/ARC/RACE-style tasks, directly analogous to CosmosQA's format.
Robust, well-aligned 8B instruct model with strong zero/few-shot MCQA performance; a reliable high-baseline choice for CosmosQA.

Best measured neighborhood evidence: it appears on two relevant biomedical datasets, with EMBO/BLURB f1=0.8392 and araag2/MedNLI accuracy=0.7921. Its biomedical instruction tuning makes it the strongest fit for medical literature-review summarization despite no direct MSLR2022 evaluation.

Strong GNN recommendation and highly relevant long-context design for document-grounded generation; it has measured results on THUDM/LongBench with f1=0.5384 and AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA with f1=0.7852. Top GNN-ranked candidate with combined score 0.3049 and a medical generation track record on X-iZhang/MIMIC-CXR-RRG, where it achieved bleu=0.513 and rouge-l=0.367. Its radiology-report focus is medically relevant, but it is less directly aligned with text-only literature-review summarization.

Second-highest GNN candidate with combined score 0.2426 and solid general language understanding results, including Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.669 and allenai/quac accuracy=0.658. Very strong measured biomedical-neighborhood performance on the closest dataset, EMBO/BLURB, with f1=0.95 and accuracy=0.99. However, it is a specialized biomedical NER model rather than a summarization model, so it is a lower-confidence recommendation for MSLR2022.

This is the only model with measured results on multiple biomedical/clinical neighbors: EMBO/BLURB with f1=0.8392 and araag2/MedNLI with accuracy=0.7921. Its consistent medical-domain performance makes it the strongest fit for allenai/mslr2022 despite no direct summarization score.

It has the strongest measured result on the most similar dataset, EMBO/BLURB, with f1=0.95 and accuracy=0.99. The evidence is highly biomedical but task-indirect for literature-review summarization, so it ranks below the more broadly medical Llama2-MedTuned model.

It also performs very strongly on the closest biomedical benchmark, EMBO/BLURB, with f1=0.95. The result is compelling but comes from a single biomedical NER-oriented evaluation rather than summarization or multiple neighboring datasets.

It was measured on L4NLP/LEval, a long-context benchmark including summarization tasks, with accuracy=0.5 and f1=0.4919. The score is modest, but long-context capability is relevant for multidocument medical evidence summarization.

It shows solid biomedical performance on EMBO/BLURB with f1=0.88. This is useful domain evidence, though it is weaker than the PharmaDetect models and remains indirect for the MSLR2022 summarization setting.

Strongest relevant measured track record across QA and long-context datasets: AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA f1=0.7852, McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA f1=0.5575, THUDM/LongBench f1=0.5384, IBM/doc2dial f1=0.4076, and allenai/quac f1=0.3899. Its GNN combined score for allenai/mslr2022 is also relatively high at 0.1737.

High GNN support with combined=0.2426 for allenai/mslr2022, and solid measured performance on related text benchmarks: Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.669 and allenai/quac accuracy=0.658. The 13B size is within the constraint and gives it more capacity than the smaller Llama variants.

Despite a low GNN combined score of 0.0093, its measured evidence is strong and relevant: allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.786, allenai/hellaswag accuracy=0.698, bengaliAI/BFCL accuracy=0.67, and EleutherAI/drop f1=0.452. Weaker than the 3B and 13B candidates but has measured coverage on several relevant datasets: Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.412, allenai/quac f1=0.379, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.328. It is included as a lightweight fallback with broader evidence than the one-evaluation alternatives.
Largest capable instruct model in the list (14B) with a 1M-token context, ideal for concatenating many biomedical abstracts and producing a coherent literature-review-style summary.
Same 1M-context recipe as the 14B variant but cheaper to fine-tune/run; Qwen2.5 instruct models are among the strongest open 7B summarizers, matching MSLR2022's long multi-document input needs.

Llama-3.1-8B specifically continued-pretrained/instruction-tuned on scientific literature for retrieval-augmented scholarly synthesis, directly aligned with MSLR2022's biomedical review-generation task.

11B encoder-decoder instruction-tuned on many summarization datasets; T5-family models have historically been the strongest baselines on MSLR-style multi-document scientific summarization when fine-tuned.
Solid 8B instruct model with a 128k context window and strong general summarization/instruction-following, a reliable high-baseline for MSLR2022 multi-abstract inputs.

Among the models evaluated on mib-bench/arc_challenge, it had the best measured result with accuracy=0.3882. The dataset is less directly aligned than PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification, but this is still real measured evidence from a semantically similar neighbor.
It was measured on mib-bench/arc_challenge with accuracy=0.337, ranking second among the available models on that neighbor. This provides weaker but still grounded evidence for general NLP transfer.

This model is specialized for claim/proposition segmentation, which is plausibly useful for scientific-review text, and has measured Salesforce/rose f1=0.5193. The main weakness is that only one measured evaluation is available.

Latest-generation 14B model with improved reasoning and instruction following; expected to fine-tune strongly on aspect-score regression and accept/reject classification.

Robust, widely-validated 8B instruct model with 128K context; strong general text understanding makes it a reliable baseline for PeerRead tasks.

Strongest measured result on the most similar neighbor, allenai/squad_v2, with accuracy=0.902 and f1=0.874. This is highly relevant because QuaRTz also centers on English question answering with supporting context.
Best measured model on SeaEval/cmmlu, a multiple-choice question-answering benchmark, with accuracy=0.839. The multiple-choice format makes this strong evidence for transfer to QuaRTz.

Robust instruction-tuned 8B baseline with strong zero/few-shot MCQ accuracy; reliable performer on QuaRTz-style qualitative reasoning.
Highly capable 7B instruct model that competes with larger baselines on commonsense reasoning benchmarks, making it a strong efficient choice for QuaRTz.

Agreement candidate with strong measured evidence on PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification, achieving accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7. Its broader track record also includes PL-MTEB/cbd with accuracy=0.6811 and f1=0.5686, making it the most evidence-backed text model here.

Provides moderate measured text performance, including allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.7293, Blpeng/nsmc accuracy=0.5506, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.4889. Top-tier general-purpose embedding model that excels at retrieval, clustering, and semantic-similarity tasks—ideal for indexing and organizing a large financial news corpus.
Strong 14B general instruction-tuned LLM with excellent reasoning and summarization ability; well-suited for extracting insights, summaries, and classifications from financial news.
Robust 8B general-purpose instruction model with strong zero/few-shot capabilities for summarization, entity extraction, and sentiment classification on news text.

Widely-used 7B instruct model with solid dialogue quality, efficient training, and a long track record of successful fine-tunes on customer-service and assistant-style datasets.

Third-best measured result on Arietem/tabmwp with accuracy=0.679, very close to OctoThinker/OctoThinker-8B-Short-Base at accuracy=0.689. This provides task-aligned evidence for tabular question answering.

Excellent measured QA performance on the most similar retrieved dataset allenai/squad_v2 with accuracy=0.902 and f1=0.874. It lacks direct table evidence, so it ranks below models with measured TabMWP or math-QA strength.

Best domain match: it has measured finance results on AdaptLLM/Headline with f1=0.97, ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank with accuracy=0.87 and f1=0.87, AdaptLLM/FiQA_SA with f1=0.79, and AdaptLLM/NER with f1=0.69. This finance-specific track record is more relevant to AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA than higher GNN predictions from non-finance models.

Strong general-purpose 8B baseline with consistent measured results across reasoning and QA-style datasets: allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.786, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.761, HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA accuracy=0.726, and Joschka/big_bench_hard accuracy=0.611. Its allenai/quac f1=0.444 is directly QA-relevant, making it a robust non-domain-specialized choice.

Highest GNN-ranked eligible model and backed by strong measured QA performance, including GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options accuracy=0.74, araag2/MedMCQA accuracy=0.627, and LangAGI-Lab/medbullets accuracy=0.623. The domain is medical rather than financial, but the consistent question-answering evidence makes it promising.

Another strong 8B QA-oriented model with measured results on AIDx/USMLE accuracy=0.6704, araag2/MedQA accuracy=0.6284, and TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro accuracy=0.543. It has a high predicted-performance score, but its measured evidence is less finance-aligned than FinMA and somewhat weaker than Meerkat.

Good measured general language competence across several benchmarks, with Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.8305, EleutherAI/lambada_openai accuracy=0.7859, and SeaEval/cmmlu accuracy=0.7238. Although not finance-specific, this consistent broad capability makes it a better fifth choice than more niche or less consistent alternatives.
Largest allowed general-purpose Qwen2.5 instruct with strong math and table/QA reasoning; consistently among top open models on FinQA-style numerical reasoning benchmarks.
R1-distilled reasoning model built on Qwen2.5-14B; explicit chain-of-thought training excels at multi-step financial arithmetic that FinQA requires.
Math-specialized 7B tuned for numerical/program-of-thought reasoning; well-suited to FinQA's arithmetic program generation over tables.
Strong code generation at 14B enables program-of-thought solutions (executing arithmetic programs) which matches FinQA's evaluation format.
FinMA is explicitly instruction-tuned on financial NLP tasks including FinQA, giving strong in-domain performance despite smaller size.

Best grounded fit from a highly similar English QA benchmark: on allenai/squad_v2 it reached accuracy=0.902 and f1=0.874. This measured result is on a question-answering dataset close to Amazon-QA, so it outweighs GNN-only predictions.

Strong measured performance on another similar English QA dataset: awinml/triviaqa with accuracy=0.776. It is less directly sentence-similarity focused than the query, but the real QA result is a solid grounded signal.

The GNN recommends it and its measured record is directly relevant to sentence similarity: PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7. Its other MTEB results are mixed, including PL-MTEB/cbd accuracy=0.6811 and PL-MTEB/allegro-reviews accuracy=0.4026, so it ranks below the strongest Source A evidence.

It has a strong measured result on the sentence-pair dataset C-MTEB/LCQMC with accuracy=0.876, which is task-aligned with paraphrase and similarity mining. The main caveat is language mismatch because LCQMC and the model are Chinese while Amazon-QA is English.

This is the top GNN-ranked candidate and has several real text-task results including allenai/sciq accuracy=0.933, HuggingFaceH4/ifeval accuracy=0.5971, and EleutherAI/truthful_qa_mc accuracy=0.3905. It is not as task-specific as the sentence-similarity models and is supported only by predictions for the query.

Strongest evidence comes from allenai/squad_v2, an English QA dataset very similar to Amazon-QA, where it achieved accuracy=0.902 and f1=0.874. This is the highest-quality measured result among the close QA neighbors.
It performed well on awinml/triviaqa, another English question-answering benchmark, with accuracy=0.776. This gives direct measured support for QA-style query-answer understanding.

It was the best measured model on the closest retrieved neighbor mib-bench/arc_challenge, with accuracy=0.3882. Although the absolute score is modest, it outperformed amd/AMD-OLMo-1B at accuracy=0.337 and winglian/basilisk-4b at accuracy=0.3285 on that dataset.

It achieved accuracy=0.876 on C-MTEB/LCQMC, which is highly relevant because it is a sentence-pair semantic similarity and paraphrase-style benchmark. The main caveat is that LCQMC is Chinese while Amazon-QA is English.

It showed strong measured QA performance on CATIE-AQ/frenchQA with accuracy=0.7714 and f1=0.8874. The result is encouraging for QA behavior, though the French-language setting makes transfer to English Amazon-QA less certain.

It has the strongest GNN recommendation and a broad measured record, including allenai/sciq accuracy=0.933, HuggingFaceH4/ifeval accuracy=0.5971, ZHENGRAN/mbpp accuracy=0.524, and ChuGyouk/asdiv accuracy=0.48. Although Qiskit-specialized, its cross-task QA and reasoning evidence makes it the best-supported candidate.

This is the most directly relevant model type for an embedding or sentence-similarity dataset, with measured PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7 plus PL-MTEB/cbd accuracy=0.6811 and f1=0.5686. The weaker PL-MTEB/allegro-reviews accuracy=0.4026 and f1=0.356 keeps it below the top model despite strong task fit.

It has consistent measured results on reasoning-style QA datasets, including EleutherAI/asdiv accuracy=0.787, ChilleD/SVAMP accuracy=0.704, and Arietem/tabmwp accuracy=0.516. Its math/tool focus is not an exact Amazon-QA match, but the multi-dataset QA evidence is solid.

It shows useful measured QA-style reasoning performance on Arietem/tabmwp accuracy=0.679 and ChuGyouk/asdiv accuracy=0.672. The low EleutherAI/hendrycks_math accuracy=0.192 suggests less consistency than the higher-ranked options.

It has strong measured results on two complex QA-oriented datasets, UWNSL/mathvista accuracy=0.73 and FanqingM/MMK12 accuracy=0.645. The evidence base is smaller and more multimodal than Amazon-QA, so it is promising but less certain.
State-of-the-art general text embedding model built on Qwen2-7B, purpose-built for semantic retrieval / QA matching tasks like Amazon-QA and consistently top-ranked on MTEB retrieval.

A DistilBERT bi-encoder pre-trained with TAS-B on MS MARCO passage retrieval, an extremely close task match to Amazon-QA question–answer retrieval and a proven strong starting point for further fine-tuning.
Sentence-T5 is designed to produce high-quality sentence embeddings and transfers well to QA-style semantic similarity/retrieval; a lightweight but strong bi-encoder base for Amazon-QA.
RoBERTa-large already fine-tuned on SQuAD2 QA, giving it strong question-answer semantic representations that adapt well when further fine-tuned as a bi-encoder on Amazon-QA pairs.
A robust, widely used encoder backbone that is the canonical starting point for training sentence-embedding / retrieval models on QA-pair datasets like Amazon-QA via contrastive fine-tuning.

Strong fit because it was the best measured model on McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA, a conversational open-domain QA dataset similar to EmpatheticDialogues, with f1=0.5575. Its ChatQA specialization makes it especially relevant for dialogue-style interaction.

It achieved the top reported result on allenai/quac with accuracy=0.658, and QuAC is an English information-seeking dialogue benchmark. The chat-tuned 13B format is a good match for conversational response tasks under the 14B limit.

It has the strongest single measured score in the neighborhood, accuracy=0.8651 on McGill-NLP/FaithDial, which is a knowledge-grounded dialogue dataset focused on faithful conversational responses. I rank it below the generative chat models because it appears more specialized as a faithfulness critic.

It was measured on McGill-NLP/FaithDial with accuracy=0.5908, providing grounded evidence on a close dialogue benchmark. As an instruction-tuned 7B model, it is more broadly usable for empathetic dialogue generation than task-specific classifiers.

It achieved accuracy=0.613 on allenai/quac, a context-dependent dialogue QA dataset, giving relevant measured support. Although weaker than the 13B Llama-2 chat result on the same dataset, it remains a strong lightweight conversational candidate.

Best measured model on McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA with f1=0.5575, a conversational open-domain QA dataset with topic switching. Its chat-QA specialization makes it a strong fit for EmpatheticDialogues-style conversational QA and response modeling.

Tied for best measured result on allenai/quac with accuracy=0.658, an English information-seeking dialogue QA benchmark. The chat-tuned 13B format is directly relevant to open-domain dialogue settings.

Highest measured score on the closest evaluated neighbor McGill-NLP/FaithDial with accuracy=0.8651. I rank it below general chat models because it is a specialized faithfulness critic rather than a dialogue generation model.

On McGill-NLP/FaithDial it achieved accuracy=0.5908, ahead of KoboldAI/OPT-13B-Nerys-v2 at accuracy=0.5745. Its instruction tuning should transfer reasonably to conversational response tasks despite only single-neighbor evidence.

Measured on allenai/quac with accuracy=0.613, the best tier among 7B chat Llama-2 variants listed there. It is weaker than the 13B Llama-2 chat result but remains a relevant compact dialogue-oriented option.

Best fit by task orientation because it is fine-tuned for multi-turn conversations, and it has strong measured general-language results on Rowan/hellaswag with accuracy=0.7934 and allenai/ai2_arc with accuracy=0.5418. The weak EleutherAI/drop f1=0.0657 is a concern, but dialogue relevance makes it the strongest candidate.

Good measured consistency across three evaluations, including allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.7293, Blpeng/nsmc accuracy=0.5506, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.4889. Its GNN predicted-performance is also relatively strong at 0.6402, supporting it as a robust general text-generation option.

Has the broadest solid measured track record among the higher-GNN candidates, with SeaEval/cmmlu accuracy=0.5707, shuyuej/MedQA-MCMLE-Benchmark accuracy=0.5493, RUCAIBox/gaokao-bench accuracy=0.4747, and SaylorTwift/bbh accuracy=0.4156. This consistency across four datasets offsets the lack of direct dialogue measurements.

Shows strong measured capability on RUCAIBox/gaokao-bench with accuracy=0.722 and a usable result on Joschka/big_bench_hard with accuracy=0.428. Its GNN predicted-performance is high at 0.7256, though the low link score makes this a less certain fit for empathetic dialogue.

Task fit is helped by its instruction-tuned dialogue orientation, and it has measured results on google/IFEval with accuracy=0.595, Rowan/hellaswag with accuracy=0.412, and allenai/quac with f1=0.379. The smaller 1B size and lower allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.328 keep it below the stronger 6B-7B options.

Largest allowed strong general-purpose chat model with excellent instruction-following and conversational quality; consistently top-tier on open-ended dialogue benchmarks, making it ideal for empathetic response generation.
Google's 9B instruction-tuned model with strong RLHF alignment; known for warm, natural, and safe conversational style well-suited to empathetic listener responses.
Meta's flagship 8B chat model with extensive RLHF; produces fluent, contextually-appropriate dialogue and handles emotional/social nuance well.
Strong 7B chat model from Qwen2.5 family with excellent multi-turn dialogue ability and instruction adherence, an efficient yet capable choice for empathetic response fine-tuning.
Well-established 7B instruction-tuned model widely used as a fine-tuning base for dialogue tasks; solid baseline for empathetic conversation modeling on this dataset.

Best measured evidence on the closest evaluated neighbor: Yelp/yelp_review_full has cosine similarity 0.7497 to the query and this model achieved f1=0.988. It is directly aligned with review sentiment classification and substantially outperforms other measured neighborhood models.

Strong measured result on the closest review-sentiment neighbor Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.979. It is slightly behind the large variant but still has excellent direct evidence for sentiment classification on similar review text.

Also measured on the closest neighbor Yelp/yelp_review_full and achieved accuracy=0.967. Although the metric differs from the top two and the model is smaller, the result is still very strong on a highly similar sentiment dataset.

The GNN predicts strong suitability with predicted-performance=0.7755, and the model has consistent measured sentiment results across several datasets: SEACrowd/uit_vsfc f1=0.7953, SEACrowd/uit_viocd f1=0.7813, and visolex/ViSFD f1=0.6698. Its evidence is less direct for English Amazon polarity but useful if the bilingual or Vietnamese-translated setting matters.

This model has measured Source A evidence on another sentiment-related neighbor, Chow05/SemEval-2014-Task-4, with f1=0.8632. The task is more aspect/token-oriented than Amazon polarity, so it ranks below the Yelp-proven models despite solid sentiment performance.
Best direct match: it achieved f1=0.988 on Yelp/yelp_review_full, an English review sentiment dataset with high similarity to the query dataset.
Very strong direct evidence from Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.979, indicating excellent transfer potential for binary Amazon review sentiment classification.
Strong measured result on the highly similar Yelp/yelp_review_full review sentiment task with accuracy=0.967, though below the larger DeBERTa zero-shot variants.
Task-relevant sentiment evidence from Chow05/SemEval-2014-Task-4 with f1=0.8632, but the dataset is less similar and focused on aspect-based sentiment rather than full-review polarity.
It has strong general text-classification evidence on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.94, but SNLI is an NLI dataset rather than a review sentiment benchmark, so transfer confidence is lower.

Best task match: it is a Vietnamese sentiment model with consistent measured results on several Vietnamese sentiment datasets, including SEACrowd/uit_vsfc accuracy=0.7637 and f1=0.7953, SEACrowd/uit_viocd accuracy=0.7468 and f1=0.7813, and visolex/ViSFD accuracy=0.679 and f1=0.6698. Its GNN predicted-performance is also high at 0.7755.

This appears to be the same Vietnamese PhoBERT sentiment specialization and has direct measured evidence on SEACrowd/uit_viocd accuracy=0.7468 and f1=0.7813 plus SEACrowd/vlsp2016_sa accuracy=0.6165 and f1=0.6001. It is ranked below wonrax/phobert-base-vietnamese-sentiment because it has fewer recorded evaluations.

Strong SEA-oriented general model with a directly relevant measured sentiment result on aisingapore/NLU-Sentiment-Analysis f1=0.8472. It also shows useful multilingual capability on aisingapore/NLG-Machine-Translation chrf=0.6671 and aisingapore/NLU-Question-Answering f1=0.7223.

Promising multilingual Southeast Asian instruction model, though without direct sentiment evidence in the record. Its measured results are strong on SeaEval/cross_mmlu accuracy=0.847, with additional results on SeaEval/cross_logiqa accuracy=0.591 and SeaEval/cn_eval accuracy=0.514.

Less directly aligned to Vietnamese text sentiment, but it meets the 14B limit and has a strong measured record across several evaluations, including asuglia/coco_pope accuracy=0.892, NCSOFT/K-MMBench accuracy=0.877, NCSOFT/K-DTCBench accuracy=0.783, and NCSOFT/K-SEED accuracy=0.772. Its GNN predicted-performance is also relatively high at 0.7687.

DeBERTa-v3-large is SOTA for text classification at its size; this zero-shot variant is pre-tuned on NLI/classification and fine-tunes exceptionally well on binary sentiment tasks like Amazon Polarity.

ModernBERT-Large is a modern encoder with long context and strong classification performance; the instruct-tuned variant adapts easily to sentiment tasks and typically matches or exceeds DeBERTa on such benchmarks.
DeBERTa-v3-large fine-tuned on multiple NLI datasets provides excellent transfer to binary sentiment classification, with proven strong performance on polarity-style tasks.
One of the strongest sub-15B LLMs; when fine-tuned or used with few-shot prompting on Amazon Polarity it achieves top-tier accuracy, though at higher compute cost than encoders.
Well-established 8B instruction-tuned LLM with strong general language understanding; fine-tuning on Amazon Polarity yields very high accuracy and it also performs well few-shot.

Strong zero-shot text-classification fit for DBpedia14 topic labels, with high measured results on Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.988 and solid transfer evidence on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank f1=0.691 and allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.644. The GNN also predicts a high normalized performance of 0.7830.

Consistent measured text-classification track record across several datasets, including OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.787, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.656, PolyAI/banking77 f1=0.567, and AmazonScience/massive f1=0.518. Its GNN predicted-performance score is also strong at 0.7510.

A smaller but still strong zero-shot classifier with excellent measured performance on Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.979 and good results on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.751. It also has relevant multi-domain evidence from AmazonScience/massive f1=0.512 and PolyAI/banking77 f1=0.421.

This is the GNN's top listed candidate with combined score 0.0861 and predicted-performance 0.6397, making it the most graph-plausible zero-shot recommendation. Its measured record includes OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.751, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.571, and AmazonScience/massive f1=0.428.

This model has direct measured evidence on the closest retrieved neighbor, heegyu/news-category-dataset, which is a topical news/document classification task similar in spirit to DBpedia14, with accuracy=0.7073 and f1=0.608. The performance is moderate, but the dataset match is the strongest measured neighborhood evidence.

Best task match: on heegyu/news-category-dataset, a close topic/news classification neighbor, it achieved accuracy=0.7073 and f1=0.608. Although the score is moderate, the dataset is the most semantically similar measured text-classification evidence for DBpedia14.

Strong measured text-classification result on CogComp/trec with accuracy=0.974 and f1=0.9784. TREC is less like DBpedia14 than news/topic classification, but the model shows excellent performance on an English multi-class classification task.

Performed well on the English question-classification dataset CogComp/trec with accuracy=0.946. The evidence is measured and classification-related, though the short-question domain is less aligned with DBpedia14 document/topic classification.

Shows strong NLP classification-style performance on elenanereiss/german-ler with f1=0.8567 and accuracy=0.9846. Confidence is limited because the evidence is German legal NER rather than English document topic classification.

Included only as a low-confidence fallback: on Stanford/web_questions it achieved accuracy=0.02264, which is weak but better than bigscience/bloom-1b1 on the same dataset. The evidence is QA rather than DBpedia-style classification, so expected fit is poor.

Strongest measured text-classification profile: OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.787, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.656, PolyAI/banking77 f1=0.567, google/trueteacher f1=0.538, and AmazonScience/massive f1=0.518. Banking77 and MASSIVE are especially relevant multi-class intent/topic-style tasks.

Very strong and consistent measured results across text datasets, including Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.988, ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank f1=0.691, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.644, and AmazonScience/massive f1=0.526. Its GNN predicted-performance is also high at 0.7830, supporting its fit despite low link probability.

Although evaluated on fewer datasets, its measured text-classification results are strong: google/trueteacher accuracy=0.866, Hate-speech-CNERG/hatexplain accuracy=0.769, and PolyAI/banking77 accuracy=0.722. The Banking77 result is a useful signal for DBpedia-style multi-class classification.

Good measured coverage across several text datasets, with Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.979, OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.751, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.544, AmazonScience/massive f1=0.512, and PolyAI/banking77 f1=0.421. It is weaker than the DeBERTa-large variants but still consistently relevant.

This model has by far the strongest GNN combined score for the query at 0.0861 and real measured text results including OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.751, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.571, MoritzLaurer/cap_sotu f1=0.479, google/trueteacher f1=0.469, and AmazonScience/massive f1=0.428. Its measured scores are lower than the DeBERTa options, so it ranks fifth despite the strong prediction.
DeBERTa-v3-large explicitly fine-tuned for zero-shot classification; excels at topic classification tasks like DBpedia-14 with strong out-of-the-box or fine-tuned accuracy.
DeBERTa-v3-large heavily trained on NLI datasets, providing an excellent starting point for topic classification via entailment or fine-tuning on DBpedia's 14 classes.
ModernBERT-large is a modern efficient encoder with strong representations, well-suited for fine-tuning on a large, clean classification dataset like DBpedia-14.
Another DeBERTa-v3-large zero-shot variant trained across 33 classification datasets, giving robust generalization to DBpedia's topical categories.
Strongest general-purpose LLM under 14B in the list; can reliably classify DBpedia-14 topics via few-shot prompting or LoRA fine-tuning, though heavier than needed.

Best measured result on the closest neighbor Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.988. This is highly relevant because Yelp/yelp_review_full is a Yelp review sentiment dataset very close to the query Yelp polarity task.

Strong measured result on the closest neighbor Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.979. It is slightly behind the large variant but still has excellent direct evidence on Yelp review sentiment classification.

Measured accuracy=0.967 on Yelp/yelp_review_full, the most similar retrieved dataset. Although weaker than the larger DeBERTa variants, it still shows strong performance on highly relevant Yelp sentiment data.
Measured accuracy=0.9131 on SetFit/SentEval-CR, a customer review sentiment dataset. This is relevant to Yelp polarity, though the evidence is from a less similar neighbor than Yelp/yelp_review_full.

Measured f1=0.8632 on Chow05/SemEval-2014-Task-4, a sentiment-focused benchmark. The task is less directly matched because it involves aspect/token-level sentiment, but it provides grounded sentiment-analysis evidence.

Best measured result on the closest neighbor, Yelp/yelp_review_full, with f1=0.988. This is highly relevant because it is Yelp review sentiment classification, closely matching fancyzhx/yelp_polarity.
Very strong measured result on Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.979. It is slightly behind the large variant but supported by the most directly relevant Yelp sentiment evidence.

Strong measured performance on the closest neighbor, Yelp/yelp_review_full, with accuracy=0.967. Although below the larger DeBERTa models, it is still directly validated on highly similar Yelp review sentiment data.

Measured accuracy=0.9131 on SetFit/SentEval-CR, an English customer-review sentiment dataset. The score is lower and the neighbor is less similar than Yelp/yelp_review_full, but the task and domain remain relevant.

Measured f1=0.8632 on Chow05/SemEval-2014-Task-4, which involves sentiment analysis but is more aspect/token-oriented than Yelp polarity classification. It is a plausible fallback, though the evidence is less directly aligned than review-level sentiment benchmarks.

This has the most task-similar measured evidence, with strong classification/sentiment-style results on allegro/klej-polemo2-in accuracy=0.909, allegro/klej-polemo2-out accuracy=0.804, allegro/klej-psc accuracy=0.989, and allegro/klej-cdsc-e accuracy=0.945. The main caution is that these are Polish KLEJ datasets rather than English Yelp reviews.

This Hermes/Mistral 7B variant has a consistent measured general NLP track record across several datasets, including NousResearch/func-calling-eval accuracy=0.91, NousResearch/json-mode-eval accuracy=0.84, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.723, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.6272, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.5461. Although not sentiment-specific, the broad English language performance makes it a strong candidate for Yelp polarity.

It shares the same strong measured Hermes/Mistral-style record, including NousResearch/func-calling-eval accuracy=0.91, NousResearch/json-mode-eval accuracy=0.84, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.723, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.6272, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.5461. This consistency across multiple text benchmarks supports it as a promising general-purpose classifier candidate.

This model shows the same robust measured results as the Hermes-2-Pro-Mistral family, with NousResearch/func-calling-eval accuracy=0.91, NousResearch/json-mode-eval accuracy=0.84, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.723, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.6272, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.5461. Its evidence is not directly from sentiment datasets, but the breadth of text-task performance is favorable.

The canonical Hermes-2-Pro-Mistral-7B-GGUF entry has consistent measured results on NousResearch/func-calling-eval accuracy=0.91, NousResearch/json-mode-eval accuracy=0.84, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.723, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.6272, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.5461. It is a strong fallback despite lacking direct Yelp or sentiment-specific measurements.

DeBERTa-v3-large is the go-to encoder for text classification and consistently achieves ~98%+ accuracy on Yelp Polarity when fine-tuned; this checkpoint is already tuned on broad NLI/classification data giving strong initialization.
Same strong DeBERTa-v3-large backbone with extensive NLI pretraining that transfers well to binary sentiment; excellent fine-tuning starting point for Yelp Polarity.

ModernBERT-large is a state-of-the-art modern encoder (long context, improved architecture) that matches or exceeds DeBERTa-v3 on many classification benchmarks and is well-suited for review-length Yelp inputs.
Commercially-licensed variant of the same DeBERTa-v3-large zeroshot model; equally strong baseline for fine-tuning on Yelp Polarity's binary label.

Largest strong general LLM in the candidate list; when fine-tuned (or even few-shot prompted) it reaches near-SOTA on sentiment tasks, offering a heavier alternative that also handles long/nuanced reviews well.

This is the only Source A model measured on DFKI-SLT/scifact, a close claim-verification dataset, with accuracy=0.76 and f1=0.436. Its real result on a fact-checking benchmark makes it the most grounded match for fever/fever.

The GNN ranked this highest among text-relevant candidates, and its measured NLI track record is strong: SebastiaanBeekman/hans accuracy=1, stanfordnlp/snli accuracy=0.94, and alisawuffles/WANLI accuracy=0.77. FEVER labels are naturally related to entailment, contradiction, and unknown evidence decisions.

This model is explicitly designed for checking whether a claim is supported by a document, matching FEVER’s core setup. Its measured result on lytang/LLM-AggreFact is accuracy=0.774, stronger than the other MiniCheck variant listed.

Source A shows a strong real classification result on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic with f1=0.787. Although wiki_toxic is less directly related than scifact, this zero-shot DeBERTa model is well suited to mapping claims into FEVER-style labels.

This is another task-aligned fact-checking model, with a measured lytang/LLM-AggreFact accuracy=0.637. It is weaker than Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B on the same benchmark but remains relevant because its input format is document-plus-claim verification.

Strongest fit because it was measured on DFKI-SLT/scifact, the closest claim-verification neighbor to FEVER, with accuracy=0.76 and f1=0.436. Its scientific claim-verification evidence is more directly relevant than generic classification or language-modeling results.

Best measured English classification result among the zero-shot models, with f1=0.787 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic. Although toxicity differs from FEVER, the model family is designed for zero-shot classification/NLI-style decisions, which is relevant to Supported/Refuted/NotEnoughInfo labeling.

Showed solid measured performance on the English Wiki Toxic classification neighbor with f1=0.751. It is slightly weaker than the large DeBERTa variant but remains a plausible FEVER candidate because zero-shot classification transfers better than unrelated generation or sentiment tasks.

Matched the DeBERTa-base zero-shot result on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic with f1=0.751, giving useful English text-classification evidence. It ranks just below the DeBERTa alternatives due to no stronger measured result in the neighborhood.

Has task-aligned NLI-style evidence on GETALP/flue with accuracy=0.7745 and f1=0.7745. Confidence is limited because FLUE is French rather than English, but the NLI framing is more relevant to FEVER than the very low WebQuestions or language-modeling results.

Best fit because FEVER is close to NLI and fact verification, and this model has strong measured NLI results: SebastiaanBeekman/hans accuracy=1, stanfordnlp/snli accuracy=0.94, and alisawuffles/WANLI accuracy=0.77. It also has the highest relevant GNN combined score among text models at 0.0097.

Directly aligned with claim support verification, with measured lytang/LLM-AggreFact accuracy=0.774. Although it has only one recorded evaluation, that dataset is highly relevant to FEVER-style factual consistency checking.

Also purpose-built for document-grounded fact checking and claim support prediction, with measured lytang/LLM-AggreFact accuracy=0.637. Its evidence is weaker than Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B but the task match is strong.

Not FEVER-specific, but it has multiple measured QA/factual reasoning results including araag2/PubMedQA accuracy=0.734, GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options accuracy=0.644, and afrimedqa/afrimedqa_v2 accuracy=0.52. The medical-domain bias makes it a weaker general FEVER candidate.

This is a text model with some measured reasoning performance, including allenai/hellaswag accuracy=0.6095, allenai/swag accuracy=0.561, and allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.328. However, its cybersecurity specialization and lack of NLI or fact-verification evaluations make it a lower-confidence choice.
Explicitly fine-tuned on FEVER along with MNLI/ANLI/LingNLI/WANLI; DeBERTa-v3-large is SOTA-class for NLI and this exact checkpoint targets the FEVER label space.
Purpose-built claim-vs-evidence fact-checking model with strong reported performance on grounded verification benchmarks, directly aligned with FEVER's task formulation.
MiniCheck was designed for evidence-grounded fact verification; Flan-T5-Large backbone offers strong entailment reasoning and is a proven FEVER-aligned checkpoint.
DeBERTa-v3-large trained on a broad NLI mixture for zero-shot classification transfers extremely well to FEVER's 3-way entailment structure.
Cross-encoder DeBERTa-v3-large NLI model naturally handles claim-evidence pair scoring, a strong general-purpose baseline for FEVER-style entailment.
Strongest overall because it has agreement support and broad biomedical tuning. It scored f1=0.8392 on EMBO/BLURB and accuracy=0.7921 on araag2/MedNLI, with a high GNN combined score of 0.6833.

Excellent measured biomedical performance on the closest medical benchmark, with f1=0.95 and accuracy=0.99 on EMBO/BLURB. It is specialized for medical entity recognition, which is relevant to medical terminology despite being narrower than a general classifier.
Very strong measured evidence on EMBO/BLURB with f1=0.95, matching the best biomedical benchmark result in Source A. It is also in the agreement set, though its GNN combined score is low at 0.0087.
Good biomedical-domain measured performance with f1=0.88 on EMBO/BLURB. It appears in both sources, but it is more narrowly focused on gene and protein entities than the broader medical-terms query.

Best direct classification-style evidence from the retrieved neighborhood, with accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7 on PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification. Its broader track record is mixed, including accuracy=0.6811 and f1=0.5686 on PL-MTEB/cbd, so it ranks below the stronger biomedical models.
Best measured biomedical result: on EMBO/BLURB it achieved f1=0.95 and accuracy=0.99. This is the strongest grounded evidence for medical text understanding among the available <=14B models.

On the biomedical EMBO/BLURB benchmark it matched the top f1=0.95 result. Although accuracy was not reported, the high measured F1 on a closely related medical NLP benchmark makes it a strong candidate.

This model scored f1=0.88 on EMBO/BLURB, giving solid measured evidence in biomedical language processing. Its domain fit is strong for medical terminology, though the score is below the PharmaDetect models.

On EMBO/BLURB it achieved f1=0.8392, showing useful biomedical adaptation in a 7B model. Its broader medical tuning may transfer well to medical Wikipedia-term classification despite lower measured performance than the OpenMed models.

This model has the strongest measured classification-style evidence outside BLURB, with accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7 on PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification. The dataset is less explicitly biomedical, but the task alignment with classification supports including it.

Best overall fit for a medical text dataset: it has strong measured results on EMBO/BLURB with f1=0.8392 and araag2/MedNLI with accuracy=0.7921. Its high GNN combined score of 0.6833 further supports the recommendation.

It has the highest GNN combined score in the filtered evidence at 0.6965 and a broad measured medical track record, including araag2/PubMedQA accuracy=0.734, Voxel51/SLAKE f1=0.723, and GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options accuracy=0.644. The evidence is consistent across several medical datasets, though some results such as afrimedqa/afrimedqa_v2 accuracy=0.52 are more moderate.

A strong medical-domain candidate with measured performance on araag2/PubMedQA at accuracy=0.776 and GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options at accuracy=0.5947. Its GNN combined score of 0.5539 is lower than the top two but still substantial.

Measured reasoning performance is very strong on GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options-hf with accuracy=0.8515 and TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro with accuracy=0.7726. The lower confidence comes from its much weaker TsinghuaC3I/MedXpertQA accuracy=0.2297 and low GNN combined score of 0.0247.

BioLinkBERT-large is a biomedical text model with measured bigbio/jnlpba f1=0.8006, making it a plausible fit for medical-term-oriented data. Confidence is lower because the evidence lists only one measured evaluation and its GNN combined score is modest at 0.0328.
Llama-3.1-8B fine-tuned on UltraMedical corpus; state-of-the-art open medical LLM at this size with strong performance on medical QA and terminology tasks.
Purpose-built biomedical Llama-3-8B, top-ranked open biomedical model on MedQA/MedMCQA, ideal for Wikipedia medical term understanding and definition generation.
Medical reasoning LLM based on Qwen2.5-7B, extensively trained on medical literature and QA, excellent for structured medical term explanation.
Clinical Llama-3-8B tuned by m42; strong benchmark performance on medical knowledge tasks and terminology comprehension.
Aloe is a competitive open medical Llama-3-8B tuned with curated biomedical instructions, well-suited for Wikipedia-style medical text tasks.
Best direct fit: it achieved f1=0.836 on cirimus/super-emotion, a large multi-label emotion dataset that explicitly aggregates GoEmotions along with other emotion corpora.
Strong task match with real measured performance: f1=0.7169 on araoye01/sem_eval_2018_task_1, a multi-label emotion classification benchmark over social-media text.

It is the GNN's top-ranked candidate and has relevant measured text-classification evidence, including f1=0.644 on allenai/social_bias_frames and f1=0.988 on Yelp/yelp_review_full. Its zero-shot multi-label classification setup is plausible for GoEmotions' 27 emotion labels.

Consistent measured results across similar English social-text classification datasets: f1=0.787 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.656 on allenai/social_bias_frames. Although not GNN-recommended here, its measured neighborhood performance is stronger than most alternatives.

Supported by both sources and has repeated measured evidence on nearby text classification tasks: f1=0.751 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.571 on allenai/social_bias_frames. It is weaker than the DeBERTa variants but remains a credible compact zero-shot baseline.

Best direct evidence from the closest evaluated emotion benchmark: on cirimus/super-emotion, a large multi-label emotion dataset that includes GoEmotions-derived data, it achieved f1=0.836. This is the highest measured score on the most semantically aligned text-emotion dataset.

Strong task match for multi-label emotion classification: on araoye01/sem_eval_2018_task_1, it achieved f1=0.7169. SemEval emotion tweets are less Reddit-like than GoEmotions but still directly measure multi-label affect recognition.

Best consistent zero-shot text-classification evidence across related social text datasets, with f1=0.787 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.656 on allenai/social_bias_frames. Although not emotion-specific, its robust performance across multiple nearby datasets makes it a strong fallback.

Shows consistent measured performance across two related classification datasets, with f1=0.751 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.571 on allenai/social_bias_frames. It is weaker than the DeBERTa large zero-shot model but still has multi-dataset evidence.

Has repeated measured evidence on related text classification tasks, scoring f1=0.751 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.544 on allenai/social_bias_frames. Its social-bias result is modest, but the two-dataset coverage makes it more reliable than single-dataset or vision-based candidates.

Best task fit because it is explicitly a zero-shot text classification model and has measured classification results across several datasets, including Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.988, ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank f1=0.691, and allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.644. It also appears at the top of the GNN recommendations with predicted-performance 0.6006.

Another explicit zero-shot text classification model with relevant measured F1 evidence, including OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.751, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.571, and google/trueteacher f1=0.469. Its track record is lower than the DeBERTa variant but still directly aligned with emotion-label classification.

Although safety-focused rather than emotion-focused, it has very consistent measured English text classification F1 results: AlignmentResearch/XSTest f1=0.82, PKU-Alignment/BeaverTails f1=0.81, and PKU-Alignment/PKU-SafeRLHF f1=0.8. Its GNN predicted-performance is also the highest among the listed models at 0.6756.

This model shows similarly strong and consistent measured risk-classification performance, with AlignmentResearch/XSTest f1=0.85, PKU-Alignment/BeaverTails-Evaluation f1=0.8, AlignmentResearch/HarmBench f1=0.8, and PKU-Alignment/PKU-SafeRLHF f1=0.77. It is less directly suited to arbitrary emotion labels than the zero-shot classifiers, but the measured F1 evidence is strong.

This is not a dedicated emotion classifier, but it has a relatively consistent measured NLP understanding record, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.762, allenai/qasc accuracy=0.685, allenai/ropes f1=0.67, and allenai/quoref f1=0.635. Its GNN predicted-performance of 0.6499 is also competitive, making it a reasonable fifth choice after more classification-aligned models.

Directly trained for multi-label emotion classification on social-media English, matching GoEmotions' task formulation and domain almost exactly; strongest out-of-the-box fit and an excellent fine-tuning starting point.
DeBERTa-v3-large is consistently top-tier for fine-tuned text classification, and this NLI/zero-shot variant transfers exceptionally well to fine-grained multi-label tasks like GoEmotions.
ModernBERT-large is a modern, high-capacity encoder that matches or beats DeBERTa on many GLUE/classification tasks and fine-tunes efficiently for multi-label emotion classification on short texts.
ModernBERT-base already fine-tuned on emotion classification data provides strong warm-start weights for GoEmotions with low compute cost and competitive accuracy.
DeBERTa-v3-large pretrained on rich NLI corpora offers strong semantic representations that transfer well to nuanced 28-class multi-label emotion detection when fine-tuned on GoEmotions.

Most directly aligned with English paraphrase identification: it was measured on SetFit/mrpc, a Microsoft Research Paraphrase Corpus variant, with accuracy=0.7293. This is the closest real evidence to PAWS among the listed results.

It achieved the strongest measured sentence-pair semantic result in the neighborhood, with accuracy=0.876 on C-MTEB/LCQMC, a paraphrase and semantic similarity dataset. The main caveat is that LCQMC is Chinese while PAWS is English.

It has high measured performance on GETALP/flue with f1=0.83, and FLUE includes PAWS-X-style paraphrasing along with related classification and NLI tasks. Although French-specific, the task family is highly relevant to PAWS.

This is the only agreement candidate, appearing in both the GNN ranking and Source A, and it has strong measured results on CATIE-AQ/frenchQA with accuracy=0.7714 and f1=0.8874. Its support is less task-aligned because the measured dataset is French question answering rather than paraphrase detection.

It was measured on projecte-aina/Parafraseja, an explicit paraphrase detection dataset, with accuracy=0.6625. The task match is strong, though the evidence is Catalan rather than English and the score is lower than the top sentence-pair candidates.

Best direct English paraphrase evidence: on SetFit/mrpc, a close paraphrase-identification benchmark, it achieved accuracy=0.7293. Its sentence-transformer design is also well aligned with PAWS-style sentence-pair semantic similarity.
Strong measured result on GETALP/flue with f1=0.83, and FLUE includes PAWS-X-style paraphrase/sentence-pair tasks. The main caveat is that the evidence is French rather than English.

Highest measured score on a sentence-pair semantic similarity benchmark: C-MTEB/LCQMC accuracy=0.876. This is task-relevant to PAWS, but the evidence is Chinese, so transfer to English PAWS is uncertain.

Direct paraphrase-detection evidence from projecte-aina/Parafraseja, where it achieved accuracy=0.6625 and led the evaluated models on that dataset. The task match is good, though the dataset is Catalan rather than English.

Among English general-purpose models, it was tied for the best measured result on the nearest neighbor allenai/quac with accuracy=0.658. The evidence is indirect because QuAC is QA/dialogue rather than paraphrase identification, but it supports broad English text understanding.

Best fit among the evidence for an English text understanding task: it has strong measured results on PatronusAI/HaluBench with accuracy=0.829 and DataRobot-Research/financebench with accuracy=0.725. Its Llama-3-8B-Instruct base and English focus make it more plausible for PAWS than the medical, multimodal, or non-English alternatives.

Shows consistent measured English QA/reasoning performance across three datasets: araag2/PubMedQA accuracy=0.772, HPAI-BSC/CareQA accuracy=0.6756, and GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options accuracy=0.6229. Although medical-domain, the repeated text-reasoning track record is stronger than most candidates.

Has the broadest measured record among high-scoring candidates, including Voxel51/SLAKE accuracy=0.831, araag2/PubMedQA accuracy=0.766, bahuang123456/vqa-rad accuracy=0.679, LangAGI-Lab/medbullets accuracy=0.562, and MMMU/MMMU accuracy=0.54. The domain is medical and partly multimodal, so transfer to PAWS is uncertain, but the consistency is valuable.

Provides several measured language-reasoning results, including LeoLM/HellaSwag_de accuracy=0.6671, allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.5879, LeoLM/MMLU_de accuracy=0.5624, LeoLM/ArcChallenge_de accuracy=0.5375, and LeoLM/TruthfulQA_de accuracy=0.5275. The main weakness is that much of the evidence is German, but the task types are closer to PAWS than visual or narrow QA-only models.

Despite modest scores, its measured evaluations are on English commonsense NLP benchmarks that are reasonably relevant to sentence-level understanding: allenai/hellaswag accuracy=0.6095, allenai/swag accuracy=0.561, and allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.328. It is ranked below the others because performance is weaker and the model is cybersecurity-specialized.
DeBERTa-v3-large is state-of-the-art on PAWS-style tasks, and this checkpoint is already fine-tuned on WANLI which specifically targets the adversarial word-overlap patterns PAWS was built to test.
ModernBERT-large fine-tuned on a broad NLI mixture provides a modern encoder backbone with strong sentence-pair reasoning, well-suited to PAWS's short paraphrase judgments.
A DeBERTa-v3-large cross-encoder purpose-built for sentence-pair classification on NLI, which transfers directly and strongly to PAWS after light fine-tuning.
RoBERTa-large trained on WANLI, whose adversarial construction closely mirrors PAWS's word-swap traps, giving excellent out-of-the-box sentence-pair discrimination.
A DeBERTa-v3-large classifier trained on a large NLI/entailment mixture; its strong pair-encoding capacity fine-tunes very well on PAWS.

Strongest overall because it appears in both sources and has measured results on two similar sentiment datasets: Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.988 and ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank with f1=0.691. The GNN also recommends it for the query with predicted-performance=0.8119, adding support despite the modest FinancialPhraseBank result.

Also supported by both sources and has an excellent measured result on the similar English sentiment dataset Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.979. Its GNN predicted-performance=0.7940 and broader measured track record, including OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic with f1=0.751, make it a strong but slightly less evidenced choice than the large variant.

Source A shows a strong measured result on the similar English sentiment benchmark Yelp/yelp_review_full with accuracy=0.967. It lacks agreement with the GNN and has only one nearby measured result, so confidence is lower than for the larger DeBERTa zero-shot models.

It has a solid measured result on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank, an English expert-annotated sentiment dataset, with accuracy=0.87 and f1=0.87. The finance-domain specialization may limit transfer to poetic sentiment, so it ranks below the more general DeBERTa zero-shot models.

It is sentiment-specific and achieved accuracy=0.9661 on Kerwin11/ChnSentiCorp, a nearby sentiment-classification dataset. However, that evidence is from Chinese rather than English poetry, so the language mismatch makes it a weaker recommendation.

Best overall measured neighborhood evidence: strong on Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.988 and also evaluated on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank with f1=0.691. It is the only model with results across multiple similar datasets, making it the most grounded recommendation despite the mixed FinancialPhraseBank score.

Very strong measured result on the closely related English sentiment dataset Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.979. Although it has only one observed dataset result, the task and language match the query well.

Shows strong measured performance on Yelp/yelp_review_full with accuracy=0.967, a large English sentiment benchmark similar in task to poem_sentiment. Evidence is narrower than the larger DeBERTa variants but still directly relevant.

Has measured English sentiment evidence on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank with accuracy=0.87 and f1=0.87. The domain is financial text rather than poetry, but the dataset is small-to-medium English sentiment classification, making it a plausible fit.

Achieves high measured sentiment performance on Kerwin11/ChnSentiCorp with accuracy=0.9661. The main caveat is language mismatch because the evidence is Chinese sentiment rather than English poetry, so it ranks below the English-aligned models.

Strongest fit because it is a zero-shot text classification model with excellent measured sentiment/review performance on Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.988 and relevant sentiment evidence on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank f1=0.691. It also has broader classification evidence on allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.644 and AmazonScience/massive f1=0.526.

Very strong text-classification candidate with measured Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.979 and OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.751. Its additional results on allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.544, AmazonScience/massive f1=0.512, and PolyAI/banking77 f1=0.421 show broad classification coverage.

It has the highest useful GNN signal among text models and strong measured sentiment-like results on allegro/klej-polemo2-in accuracy=0.909 and allegro/klej-polemo2-out accuracy=0.804. The main caveat is language/domain mismatch, but its consistent Polish classification record also includes allegro/klej-psc accuracy=0.989 and allegro/klej-cdsc-e accuracy=0.945.

This is a text-to-text language model with some measured NLP classification evidence, including RussianNLP/rucola accuracy=0.7126 and RussianNLP/russian_super_glue accuracy=0.578. The evidence is less directly sentiment-related and largely Russian-language, so it is weaker for poem sentiment than the top three.

Included as a 7B text language model with some measured language ability on Helsinki-NLP/tatoeba_mt bleu=0.558 and chrf=0.707. However, it lacks direct sentiment or classification benchmarks in the evidence, making it a speculative fifth choice.

DeBERTa-v3-large is the strongest encoder for short-text sentiment classification, and this zero-shot-tuned variant fine-tunes exceptionally well on small labeled sets like poem_sentiment (~900 examples).
DeBERTa-v3-large pre-fine-tuned on a large NLI mix; the entailment prior transfers strongly to 4-class sentiment via label-verbalization or a light fine-tune.
ModernBERT-large is a modern encoder with strong short-text classification performance, ample capacity (340M), and better long-context handling than legacy BERT/RoBERTa.
Another DeBERTa-v3-large zero-shot checkpoint trained on 33 classification datasets, giving strong out-of-the-box performance on poem sentiment labels.
DeBERTa-v3-large NLI cross-encoder that can be used zero-shot for the 4 sentiment labels or fine-tuned; DeBERTa-v3-large remains the top backbone for this task size.

Best measured cross-neighborhood evidence: McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA f1=0.5575 and IBM/doc2dial f1=0.4076. Both are conversational QA/dialogue datasets close to Taskmaster-1, and this model leads both shared evaluations.

Consistent measured results on the two closest evaluated dialogue-QA datasets: McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA f1=0.4996 and IBM/doc2dial f1=0.3933. It trails nvidia/Llama3-ChatQA-2-8B but has directly relevant conversational QA evidence.

Very strong measured result on a dialogue-system-style benchmark, NousResearch/func-calling-eval accuracy=0.91. Although this evidence is from one less-similar dataset, the task format with system and user prompts is relevant to goal-oriented dialogue.

Strong measured performance on allenai/quac with accuracy=0.658, a contextual information-seeking dialogue dataset. The chat-tuned 13B model is within the parameter limit and well matched to conversational response modeling.

This is the only agreement model and has measured Source A performance on AmazonScience/massive with f1=0.428, plus Source B support at GNN rank 19. Its track record also includes OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.751, but it is a weaker fit for dialogue generation than the leading chat models.

Best and most consistent evidence across the two closest evaluated neighbors: McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA with f1=0.5575 and IBM/doc2dial with f1=0.4076. Its ChatQA orientation is well aligned with Taskmaster-1 style goal-oriented dialogues.

Strong repeated evidence on the two closest dialogue QA datasets, scoring f1=0.4996 on McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA and f1=0.3933 on IBM/doc2dial. It is slightly weaker than nvidia/Llama3-ChatQA-2-8B but remains a consistent conversational QA fit.

Also has measured results on both nearest evaluated neighbors, with accuracy=0.4996 on McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA and accuracy=0.3933 on IBM/doc2dial. This makes it a grounded fallback ChatQA-style option despite being similar to another Llama3-ChatQA variant.

Shows strong measured dialogue-QA performance on allenai/quac with accuracy=0.658, one of the more semantically similar information-seeking dialogue datasets. Its chat-tuned 13B format is relevant for Taskmaster-1 conversational modeling.

Achieved accuracy=0.91 on NousResearch/func-calling-eval, a structured dialogue and tool-use style benchmark related to goal-oriented interaction. Although the dataset similarity is lower than the top neighbors, the high measured task-oriented dialogue result makes it promising.

Top GNN recommendation and the strongest broad measured NLP record, with Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.699, EleutherAI/asdiv accuracy=0.672, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.638, and PNYX/bbh accuracy=0.552. Although code-oriented, its consistent results across reasoning and language-understanding datasets make it the best supported fit.

Strong instruction-following and generation-oriented evidence, including google/IFEval accuracy=0.6861, google-research-datasets/mbpp accuracy=0.6508, and EleutherAI/hendrycks_math accuracy=0.6062. Its instruct tuning is especially relevant for task-oriented dialogue use cases.

Broad multilingual language-model evidence with strong measured results on allenai/sciq accuracy=0.9, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.6456, and EleutherAI/lambada_openai accuracy=0.5762. It is weaker on Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.463, but the breadth of evaluations supports it as a solid general text model.

Good measured reasoning and instruction-related evidence, with ibm-research/acp_bench accuracy=0.693, CogComp/mc_taco accuracy=0.661, and HuggingFaceH4/ifeval accuracy=0.414. It is less consistently strong across all datasets, but its 14B reasoning-focused profile is promising for complex dialogue understanding.

Smaller than BLOOM-7b1 but still has a reasonably broad measured track record, including allenai/sciq accuracy=0.833, aps/super_glue accuracy=0.68, and allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.5493. Lower results on EleutherAI/lambada_openai accuracy=0.4262 and Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.3463 place it behind the stronger candidates.

The strongest general instruction-tuned model in the ≤14B list with excellent multi-turn dialogue, instruction-following, and structured output ability — ideal for Taskmaster-1's slot-filled task-oriented conversations.
A top-tier 8B instruction-tuned model with strong dialogue and reasoning skills, well-suited for multi-domain task-oriented conversations and easy to fine-tune on Taskmaster-1.
Explicitly tuned for function calling and agentic task completion, which aligns closely with Taskmaster-1's API-style slot-filling and action-taking dialogue structure.
xLAM is Salesforce's agent/function-calling series; the 8B FC variant is purpose-built for task-oriented dialogue with tool invocation, matching Taskmaster-1's structure very well.
A strong 9B instruction-tuned model with good multi-turn conversational quality and instruction-following, providing a solid alternative architecture for Taskmaster-1 modeling.
Strongest measured neighborhood evidence: it achieved f1=0.787 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.656 on allenai/social_bias_frames, both highly relevant to English toxicity and bias detection.

This is the agreement candidate, appearing in both sources; it has real measured f1=0.644 on allenai/social_bias_frames and Source B also reports f1=0.988 on Yelp/yelp_review_full and f1=0.691 on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank.
It has consistent measured results across two similar datasets, with f1=0.751 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.571 on allenai/social_bias_frames, making it a solid smaller zero-shot classifier.
It matches the roberta-base model on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic with f1=0.751, but is weaker on allenai/social_bias_frames with f1=0.544, so it ranks slightly lower.

Although supported only by the GNN source, its measured safety track record is relevant to toxicity moderation: f1=0.85 on AlignmentResearch/XSTest, f1=0.8 on PKU-Alignment/BeaverTails-Evaluation, f1=0.8 on AlignmentResearch/HarmBench, and f1=0.77 on PKU-Alignment/PKU-SafeRLHF.

Best grounded fit: it leads the most similar toxicity dataset OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic with f1=0.787 and also leads allenai/social_bias_frames with f1=0.656. This gives the strongest consistent English toxicity and bias-classification evidence.

Strong measured consistency, with f1=0.751 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.571 on allenai/social_bias_frames. Its direct English toxicity result is high, though its social-bias score trails the top DeBERTa model.

Validated on two relevant English datasets, scoring f1=0.751 on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic and f1=0.544 on allenai/social_bias_frames. It matches RoBERTa on the most similar toxicity dataset but is weaker on social bias.

Although only measured on one neighborhood dataset, it performs well on the closely related English hate/offensiveness dataset allenai/social_bias_frames with f1=0.644. Lack of measured OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic evidence makes it less certain than models validated on both datasets.

It has direct measured evidence on allenai/social_bias_frames with f1=0.571, matching the original RoBERTa model on that dataset. However, it lacks measured results on OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic, so confidence is lower.

Best match to a civil-comments toxicity or safety task: it has consistent measured safety results on AlignmentResearch/XSTest with f1=0.85, PKU-Alignment/BeaverTails-Evaluation with f1=0.8, AlignmentResearch/HarmBench with f1=0.8, and PKU-Alignment/PKU-SafeRLHF with f1=0.77.

Strong general text-classification evidence and relevant social-content evidence, including Yelp/yelp_review_full with f1=0.988 and allenai/social_bias_frames with f1=0.644. It also has multiple additional measured classification results such as ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank with f1=0.691 and AmazonScience/massive with f1=0.526.

This is the only candidate with a very strong nonzero GNN recommendation for the query dataset, combined=0.9311 with predicted-performance=0.9317. Its measured record is mixed but includes useful text-pair/classification evidence on PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification with accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7, plus PL-MTEB/cbd with accuracy=0.6811 and f1=0.5686.

Relevant because its only measured evaluation is on harmlessness-style content, HuggingFaceH4/cai-conversation-harmless with accuracy=0.6725. The evidence is much thinner than the higher-ranked models, but the task type is closer to civil-comment moderation than multimodal, medical, or protein models.

DeBERTa-v3-large already fine-tuned as a toxicity scorer — directly aligned with Civil Comments' toxic-comment labels, giving strong zero-shot performance and an excellent fine-tuning starting point.
DeBERTa-v3-large is the top encoder for text classification; NLI pretraining on multiple corpora transfers strongly when fine-tuned on toxicity labels of comment text.
ModernBERT-large is a modern, long-context encoder that matches or beats DeBERTa on many classification tasks and handles the long comment inputs in Civil Comments well.
DeBERTa-v3-large tuned for robust zero-shot classification; excellent backbone for fine-tuning binary/multi-label toxicity attributes with limited compute.
RoBERTa-base pretrained on Twitter and fine-tuned for hate-speech detection — smaller but domain-aligned to abusive online text, providing a strong efficient baseline.

Best measured model on GEM/xsum with bleu=0.153, outperforming google/byt5-small at bleu=0.091 on the same similar summarization dataset. The evidence is only from one benchmark and uses BLEU rather than ROUGE, so confidence is moderate.

Strong measured CNN/DailyMail summarization result on abisee/cnn_dailymail with rouge-2=0.2265 and rouge-l=0.2989, higher than the other models evaluated on that dataset. It is supported by only one neighbor and may be less domain-aligned than the top-ranked options.

This model has consistent measured summarization results across two relevant neighbors: EdinburghNLP/xsum with rouge-2=0.107 and rouge-l=0.2552, and abisee/cnn_dailymail with rouge-2=0.1666 and rouge-l=0.2722. THUDM/glm-10b has strong measured ROUGE on the most similar evaluated dataset, EdinburghNLP/xsum, with rouge-2=0.257 and rouge-l=0.404. Although it appears on only one neighbor, this is the strongest ROUGE evidence among the English summarization results.

google/byt5-xxl was evaluated on GEM/xsum, a similar XSum summarization benchmark, with bleu=0.153, outperforming google/byt5-small at bleu=0.091. The evidence is limited to BLEU on one neighbor, but its measured result and byte-level robustness make it a plausible option for chemistry text.

Top-tier 14B instruction-tuned LLM with 1M-token context, ideal for summarizing long chemistry papers end-to-end without truncation and strong on abstractive summarization benchmarks.

Encoder-decoder Flan-T5 XXL is a classic, highly reliable summarization model that fine-tunes efficiently on scientific abstractive summarization tasks like ChemSum.
Strong general-purpose 8B instruct model with 128k context; a widely used, robust base for fine-tuning long-document summarization with good factuality.
Pretrained on a large corpus of scientific literature including chemistry papers, giving it domain vocabulary and knowledge advantages for ChemSum-style summarization.

Strongest consistency in Source A, with real NER f1=0.974 on CATIE-AQ/frenchNER_4entities, f1=0.9818 on Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr, and f1=0.921 on MultiCoNER/multiconer_v2. It has the strongest measured NER results across multiple similar datasets: Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr f1=0.99 and MultiCoNER/multiconer_v2 f1=0.976. It achieved a very strong measured result on the similar Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr NER dataset with f1=0.98. The evidence is only from one dataset, so it is less reliable than the top two multi-dataset NER models.

It was the best model on the SEACrowd/vlsp2016_ner dataset with f1=0.947, showing strong measured performance on a web-news NER benchmark. However, this is single-dataset Vietnamese evidence, making transfer to English financial NER less certain.

It performed well on SEACrowd/vlsp2016_ner with f1=0.936, close to vinai/phobert-large on the same NER benchmark. Its evidence is narrower than the higher-ranked models because it appears only on one Vietnamese NER dataset.

Strong measured NLP track record across several tasks, including PlanTL-GOB-ES/CoNLL-NERC-es with f1=0.8823 and PlanTL-GOB-ES/MLDoc with f1=0.9702.
