This is the only candidate with direct financial-domain measured evidence, scoring f1=0.691 on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank. Its broader classification record is mixed but useful, with Yelp/yelp_review_full f1=0.988 and allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.644.

It has the most directly task-relevant measured evidence for entity recognition, with elenanereiss/german-ler f1=0.8567 and accuracy=0.9846. The main limitation is that this support comes from only one known evaluation and from German legal rather than financial text.

The GNN gave this model the strongest listed combined score, 0.0186, and it has consistent measured Polish NLP results such as allegro/klej-psc accuracy=0.989, allegro/klej-cdsc-e accuracy=0.945, and allegro/klej-polemo2-in accuracy=0.909. Its evidence is less domain- and language-aligned than the top choices, but the multi-dataset record is solid.

This 6B text model is within the parameter constraint and has some general-language measured evidence, including allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.7293. However, its other results are modest, with Blpeng/nsmc accuracy=0.5506 and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.4889, so it is a weaker fallback candidate.
Largest allowed strong general instruction-tuned model; Qwen2.5 shows top-tier zero/few-shot NER and information extraction performance on English financial text.
FinMA is explicitly domain-adapted to financial NLP tasks including NER on financial news, making it an ideal specialist for FiNER-ORD's PER/LOC/ORG labels.
Gemma-2-9B-it is among the strongest sub-10B instruction models and consistently performs well on token-level extraction and NER benchmarks.
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct offers robust instruction following and reliable entity extraction on English news text, a solid general-purpose baseline for financial NER.
Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 is a well-established 7B instruct model with strong zero/few-shot NER capability and good prompt controllability for structured extraction.
Best measured model on the closest fact-verification neighbor lytang/LLM-AggreFact with accuracy=0.774. This is the most directly relevant evidence for HoVer-style claim support verification.

Strong measured result on lytang/LLM-AggreFact with accuracy=0.738, the most semantically aligned fact-checking benchmark in Source A. Its task specialization makes it a strong candidate despite being below Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B.
Measured accuracy=0.699 on lytang/LLM-AggreFact, giving it direct evidence on a similar factual-consistency benchmark. It trails the top two but remains task-aligned for claim verification.

Measured accuracy=0.637 on lytang/LLM-AggreFact, which is lower than the other MiniCheck and FactCG models but still directly relevant to factual consistency. Its task alignment makes it preferable to higher-scoring models measured only on less relevant QA or commonsense datasets.

Strongest fit because it is the top measured model on the most similar benchmark, lytang/LLM-AggreFact, with accuracy=0.774. That dataset is explicitly fact verification/factual consistency, closely matching HoVer's supported/not-supported claim setting.

Second-best measured result on the closest benchmark, lytang/LLM-AggreFact, with accuracy=0.738. Its fact-checking orientation makes the evidence more directly relevant than higher scores from less similar QA or commonsense datasets.

A solid fact-verification candidate with measured accuracy=0.699 on lytang/LLM-AggreFact. Although below the top two on that benchmark, it is still evaluated on the most relevant neighboring dataset for HoVer.

Very strong measured QA performance on allenai/squad_v2 with accuracy=0.902 and f1=0.874. This is less directly fact-checking-specific than LLM-AggreFact, but SQuAD v2's evidence-grounded question answering is relevant to HoVer-style retrieval and verification.

Included because it has direct measured evidence on the closest fact-verification benchmark, lytang/LLM-AggreFact, with accuracy=0.637. The score is lower than the other MiniCheck/FactCG models, but the task match is stronger than results from less related benchmarks.

Has multiple measured English commonsense and reasoning evaluations, including allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.5399, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.4239, and mib-bench/arc_challenge accuracy=0.3285. Very consistent on text NLP benchmarks, with allegro/klej-psc accuracy=0.989, allegro/klej-cdsc-e accuracy=0.945, and allegro/klej-polemo2-in accuracy=0.909. It is downranked because the evidence is Polish-specific, so transfer to an English HoVer-style task is unclear.

Although primarily multimodal, it has strong measured QA/reasoning-adjacent results such as armanc/ScienceQA accuracy=0.736, HuggingFaceM4/VQAv2 accuracy=0.828, and HuggingFaceM4/POPE_modif accuracy=0.862. Top-tier open 14B instruct model with strong performance on multi-hop reasoning, long-context evidence handling, and NLI-style classification, all core skills for HoVer.

Reasoning-distilled 14B model that excels at chain-of-thought over multiple evidence chunks, which matches HoVer's multi-hop verification structure.
Strong general 8B instruct model with solid long-context and NLI performance; a proven backbone for FEVER/HoVer-style fact-checking pipelines.
Directly fine-tuned on FEVER plus multiple NLI corpora; small but highly competitive for supported/not-supported classification once evidence is retrieved.

The results suggest solid reasoning and instruction-following ability, though the measured datasets are less directly similar to SAMSum.

This 7B text-generation model has a consistent measured German benchmark record, with accuracy=0.663 on LeoLM/HellaSwag_de, accuracy=0.485 on LeoLM/ArcChallenge_de, and accuracy=0.481 on LeoLM/MMLU_de. It is less directly supported for English dialogue summarization than the higher-ranked models, but it is still a plausible compact LLM candidate.
Largest strong instruction-tuned model in the pool; Qwen2.5 excels at zero-/few-shot summarization and follows length/format instructions well, ideal for SAMSum's concise abstractive summaries.
Flan-T5 encoder-decoder is a longstanding SAMSum leader; instruction-tuned on summarization tasks and fine-tunes with very high ROUGE on dialog summarization benchmarks.
Gemma-2-9B-it is an exceptionally strong 9B instruction model with excellent summarization and instruction-following, competitive with larger models on abstractive summarization.
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is a well-aligned general-purpose model with strong summarization ability and good conversational understanding needed to summarize multi-party chats.
Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct offers near-state-of-the-art 7B summarization quality with strong instruction-following, a proven strong fine-tuning base for SAMSum-style tasks.

Strongest grounded fit from Source A: on the English summarization dataset EdinburghNLP/xsum it achieved rouge-l=0.404 and rouge-2=0.257. This is measured summarization evidence on a semantically similar benchmark, though XSum is shorter news rather than long government reports.

Top GNN recommendation for launch/gov_report with combined score 0.0253, and its track record includes THUDM/LongBench f1=0.5384 and AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA f1=0.7852. Its long-context design is especially relevant for GovReport-style long document summarization, but the evidence is predictive rather than measured summarization.

Has direct measured summarization evidence on EdinburghNLP/xsum with rouge-l=0.2552 and rouge-2=0.107. The score is below THUDM/glm-10b, but it is an explicit summarization model evaluated on an English summarization benchmark.

Second-highest GNN recommendation with combined score 0.0236, and it has solid general NLP results such as allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.786 and allenai/quac f1=0.429. It lacks measured summarization results here, so it ranks below models with real summarization evidence.

This is the only agreement candidate, appearing in both the GNN list and Source A, but its measured similar-dataset evidence is weak and indirect: ai-forever/MERA accuracy=0.092 and f1=0.315. It remains a plausible fallback because it is a 7B instruction model, but the available metrics do not strongly support it for summarization.

Best measured ROUGE evidence among the English summarization candidates: on EdinburghNLP/xsum it achieved rouge-l=0.404 and rouge-2=0.257. XSum is not long government-report summarization, but it is the strongest available measured English summarization signal.

On EdinburghNLP/xsum it achieved rouge-l=0.2552 and rouge-2=0.107, giving solid measured evidence on an English summarization task. It trails THUDM/glm-10b but remains one of the better evaluated options under the 14B constraint.

On EdinburghNLP/xsum it achieved rouge-l=0.2538 and rouge-2=0.1062, nearly matching the v2 mt5-small summarization model. The evidence is directly summarization-focused, though still from short news rather than GovReport-style long documents.

On EdinburghNLP/xsum it achieved rouge-l=0.1754, providing measured English summarization evidence. Its ROUGE-L is clearly below the top XSum models and no rouge-2 value is reported, so confidence is moderate-low.

On EdinburghNLP/xsum it achieved rouge-l=0.1569 and rouge-2=0.05863, with f1=0.5147. It is evaluated on an English summarization benchmark, but its ROUGE scores are weaker than the other XSum-based recommendations.

Strongest fit because it is explicitly long-context oriented and has the top GNN combined score 0.0253. It also has relevant measured QA/long-context evidence, including AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA f1=0.7852, McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA f1=0.5575, and THUDM/LongBench f1=0.5384.

Broadly strong measured track record across several text datasets, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.786, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.761, HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA accuracy=0.726, and allenai/quac f1=0.444. Although its GNN link score is low, the measured evidence is consistent and from a capable 8B text model.

Promising for long-document use because the model is described as long-context capable up to 200K tokens, and its GNN predicted-performance is high at 0.2054. Its measured results are solid but less directly similar, with allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.7258, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.7111, and Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.5728.

Ranks second by GNN combined score at 0.0236 and has multiple measured text-task results, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.786, Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.698, and allenai/quac f1=0.429. The smaller 3B size and quantization make it somewhat less certain for GovReport-style long outputs than the stronger 8B/9B options.

Has consistent measured QA/reading-comprehension evidence across several datasets, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.762, allenai/qasc accuracy=0.685, allenai/ropes f1=0.67, and allenai/quoref f1=0.635. It is less ideal because it is a small QA-focused T5 model rather than a long-context summarization-oriented model.
Largest allowable Qwen2.5 instruct model with native 1M-token context; state-of-the-art among ≤14B models on long-document summarization and instruction following, ideal for gov_report's long inputs.
Same 1M-context Qwen2.5 recipe at 7B; retains excellent long-doc summarization quality at lower cost, a strong efficient choice for this dataset.
Strong 128K-context instruction-tuned model with proven summarization performance and robust factual fidelity, well-suited to multi-thousand-token government reports.
GLM-4 9B chat with 1M context; competitive summarization ability and long-context robustness, a good alternative to Qwen for gov_report.
InternLM2.5-7B chat with 1M context; solid long-document comprehension and summarization, providing model diversity while comfortably handling gov_report length.

Strongest measured summarization evidence: on EdinburghNLP/xsum it achieved rouge-2=0.257 and rouge-l=0.404, the best ROUGE values among the English summarization results. XSum is one of the closest retrieved datasets to GovReport-QS with cosine similarity 0.6008.

Although GNN-only for this query, it is highly relevant for long-context question-focused document understanding and has measured results on THUDM/LongBench with f1=0.5384 plus AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA with f1=0.7852. Its GNN score is also the strongest clearly task-relevant prediction after the top-ranked MegaBeam model.

It has direct measured evidence on the similar English summarization dataset EdinburghNLP/xsum, with f1=0.5147, rouge-l=0.1569, and rouge-2=0.05863. The ROUGE scores are weaker than THUDM/glm-10b, but the measured XSum result still provides grounded support.

This summarization-specific model was measured on EdinburghNLP/xsum with rouge-2=0.107 and rouge-l=0.2552. Its evidence is grounded on a close English summarization neighbor, though its ROUGE scores trail THUDM/glm-10b.

It shows similar measured summarization performance on EdinburghNLP/xsum with rouge-2=0.1062 and rouge-l=0.2538. This is slightly below T-Systems-onsite/mt5-small-sum-de-en-v2 but still provides relevant measured evidence on a close summarization dataset.

Strongest measured summarization evidence among the candidates on EdinburghNLP/xsum, with rouge-2=0.257 and rouge-l=0.404. XSum is the closest evaluated English summarization neighbor to launch/gov_report_qs.
Shows solid measured XSum summarization performance with rouge-2=0.107 and rouge-l=0.2552. Its results are clearly below THUDM/glm-10b but stronger than most remaining English-neighbor evidence.
Very similar measured performance to the v2 model on EdinburghNLP/xsum, with rouge-2=0.1062 and rouge-l=0.2538. This makes it a reasonable backup summarization candidate for the GovReport-QS setting.

Has measured evidence on EdinburghNLP/xsum with rouge-l=0.1754, but lacks a reported rouge-2 score in the evidence. It is weaker than the mT5 summarization models but still has relevant English summarization-neighbor evaluation.

Evaluated on EdinburghNLP/xsum with rouge-2=0.05863, rouge-l=0.1569, and f1=0.5147. Its ROUGE scores are relatively low, but it remains one of the few models with real measured evidence on the closest evaluated summarization dataset.

Best fit because it has the strongest measured long-context and QA track record: AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA f1=0.7852, McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA f1=0.5575, THUDM/LongBench f1=0.5384, IBM/doc2dial f1=0.4076, and allenai/quac f1=0.3899. It also has a high GNN combined score of 0.1740 for launch/gov_report_qs.

This ChatQA-family model has consistent measured evidence on similar QA and dialogue/document tasks: AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA accuracy=0.7846, McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA accuracy=0.4996, allenai/quac accuracy=0.3973, and IBM/doc2dial accuracy=0.3933. Its GNN score is very low, but the measured task match is strong.

A dedicated QA model with broad measured QA evidence: allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.762, allenai/qasc accuracy=0.685, allenai/ropes f1=0.67, allenai/quoref f1=0.635, and allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.607. Its GNN link score is low, but the measured QA consistency makes it promising.

A strong general 8B baseline with solid measured results across reasoning and QA-style tasks, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.786, HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA accuracy=0.726, Joschka/big_bench_hard accuracy=0.611, and allenai/quac f1=0.444. It is less specialized for long-document QA than the ChatQA models.

This model has the top GNN combined score for launch/gov_report_qs at 0.1997 and a relevant long-context measured result on RMT-team/babilong with accuracy=0.482. However, it has only one known measured evaluation, so it ranks below models with broader verified QA evidence.
Top-tier 14B instruction model with a 1M-token context window, ideal for QA over long government reports without truncation, and strong on reading-comprehension/summarization benchmarks.
Largest allowed Qwen2.5 instruct model (128K context) with excellent instruction-following and long-document QA/summarization performance, well-suited to grounded answer generation.
Strong general-purpose instruction model with a 128K context, reliable long-document QA and faithful extraction, widely validated on long-context and summarization benchmarks.
7B Qwen2.5 with a 1M context—an efficient long-context QA option that handles entire government reports in a single pass while retaining strong instruction-following.
Highly capable 9B instruct model with strong reading-comprehension and summarization quality; competitive for grounded QA on structured government prose despite its 8K native context.

Most directly aligned with DailyDialog's emotion-label component: it achieved f1=0.836 on cirimus/super-emotion, a large multi-label emotion classification dataset with labels overlapping DailyDialog such as joy, sadness, anger, fear, and surprise.

Strong measured result on a closely related English dialogue benchmark: accuracy=0.8651 on McGill-NLP/FaithDial, which involves conversational turns and dialogue-response labeling. This is indirect but highly relevant to DailyDialog's dialogue understanding setting.

Although only supported by the GNN source, it is explicitly designed for zero-shot text classification and has strong measured classification results including f1=0.988 on Yelp/yelp_review_full and f1=0.644 on allenai/social_bias_frames. This makes it a plausible fit for unseen DailyDialog intent and emotion labels.

Measured on a related dialogue dataset with accuracy=0.5908 on McGill-NLP/FaithDial, giving grounded evidence for English conversational understanding. Its general instruction-tuned nature may help adapt to DailyDialog's dialog-act and emotion classification format.

Best measured model on IBM/doc2dial with f1=0.4076, a related English goal-oriented dialogue benchmark. The task is more QA-oriented than DailyDialog classification, so the evidence is weaker but still relevant for multi-turn dialogue understanding.

Strong task alignment with DailyDialog's emotion labels: it achieved f1=0.836 on cirimus/super-emotion, a large multi-label emotion classification dataset. Although the neighbor similarity is slightly lower, the measured emotion-classification evidence is directly relevant.

Best measured result on an English dialogue neighbor, with accuracy=0.8651 on McGill-NLP/FaithDial. FaithDial is a conversational dataset, making this strong evidence for dialogue-context understanding even though its labels differ from DailyDialog.

Measured on the English dialogue dataset McGill-NLP/FaithDial with accuracy=0.5908. Its result is below the task-specific RoBERTa model but still provides relevant evidence on a close conversational benchmark.

Also evaluated on McGill-NLP/FaithDial, where it achieved accuracy=0.5745. This is modest but grounded evidence from a similar English dialogue setting and remains within the 14B parameter constraint.

Best measured model on IBM/doc2dial, achieving f1=0.4076 on an English goal-oriented dialogue QA benchmark. The score is lower than the FaithDial and emotion-classification evidence, but it is still the strongest Doc2Dial result among eligible models.

Strongest text-classification fit: it has measured f1=0.988 on Yelp/yelp_review_full, f1=0.691 on ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank, and f1=0.644 on allenai/social_bias_frames. This is more directly relevant to DailyDialog-style utterance classification than most alternatives, and its GNN predicted-performance is also high at 0.9328.

Most directly conversation-related measured evidence, with accuracy=0.6725 on HuggingFaceH4/cai-conversation-harmless. The track record is only one evaluation, but the conversational alignment makes it a promising DailyDialog candidate.

Very consistent measured classification performance across several datasets, including accuracy=0.989 on allegro/klej-psc, accuracy=0.945 on allegro/klej-cdsc-e, and accuracy=0.909 on allegro/klej-polemo2-in. It is Polish-focused rather than DailyDialog-like English dialogue, so I rank it below more task-relevant options despite the high GNN predicted-performance of 0.9416.

It has by far the strongest GNN combined score among the candidates, and measured results are solid across multiple evaluations such as accuracy=0.888 on TIGER-Lab/NLVR2 and accuracy=0.627 on BLINK-Benchmark/BLINK. However, the measured evidence is mostly multimodal rather than dialogue-text specific, so it is a lower-confidence fit.

Shows stable measured performance across four multilingual reasoning benchmarks, including accuracy=0.624 on Eurolingua/hellaswagx, accuracy=0.581 on Eurolingua/arcx, and accuracy=0.543 on Eurolingua/truthfulqax. The evidence is not dialogue-specific, but the consistent language-understanding results make it a reasonable 7B fallback.

Largest strong modern instruction-tuned chat LLM in the list; excels at multi-turn dialogue generation and can be fine-tuned for dialog-act/emotion classification with top-tier results on DailyDialog.
State-of-the-art 8B chat model with strong conversational quality and instruction-following, a proven backbone for dialogue generation and classification fine-tuning.
Highly competitive 9B instruction-tuned model with strong English conversational and reasoning ability, well-suited to DailyDialog's short multi-turn chats.
Efficient 7B chat model with excellent dialogue quality and classification transfer; a strong lower-cost alternative that often matches larger baselines on DailyDialog.
Robust and widely-used 7B instruct model with solid multi-turn conversational performance and easy fine-tuning for response generation and act/emotion classification.

It has the best measured result on the closest direct analogue, GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options, with accuracy=0.74. This is strong grounded evidence for a MedQA-style multiple-choice medical exam dataset.

It performs strongly on GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options with accuracy=0.7156, the second-best non-duplicate model result in the neighborhood. It also has measured coverage on TsinghuaC3I/MedXpertQA with accuracy=0.1551, though that harder expert benchmark tempers confidence.

It is the top GNN recommendation with combined score=0.7341 and also has real results on similar medical QA datasets, including GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options accuracy=0.644 and TsinghuaC3I/MedXpertQA accuracy=0.142. Its broader track record includes araag2/PubMedQA accuracy=0.734 and afrimedqa/afrimedqa_v2 accuracy=0.52.

It appears in both sources and is the GNN rank 2 model with combined score=0.6302. Its measured evidence is strong but less directly matched to text-only MedQA, with GoodBaiBai88/M3D-VQA accuracy=0.7995.

It has direct measured evidence on the highly relevant GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options benchmark with accuracy=0.6229. Although supported by only one similar-dataset result, that result is on a close MedQA/USMLE-style task.

Best measured result on the closest text medical exam benchmark, GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options, with accuracy=0.74. This is highly relevant because the query dataset is also MedQA-style medical multiple-choice QA.
Matched the top measured performance on GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options with accuracy=0.74. As a derived GGUF version of the leading Meerkat model, it has strong direct evidence for MedQA-like tasks.

Strong direct performance on GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options with accuracy=0.7156 and additional measured evidence on TsinghuaC3I/MedXpertQA with accuracy=0.1551. The cross-dataset evidence supports it as a robust medical reasoning candidate.

Good measured performance on GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options with accuracy=0.644 and additional evidence on TsinghuaC3I/MedXpertQA with accuracy=0.142. Its consistency across medical QA benchmarks makes it a reasonable smaller-model option.

Performed competitively on the closest benchmark, GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options, with accuracy=0.6182. Although it lacks multi-dataset evidence here, the direct MedQA-style result makes it more relevant than models evaluated only on less similar multimodal benchmarks.

Best overall fit because it has the top GNN combined score 0.7341 and directly relevant measured medical QA results: araag2/PubMedQA accuracy=0.734 and GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options accuracy=0.644. It also has broader medical evidence on Voxel51/SLAKE f1=0.723 and afrimedqa/afrimedqa_v2 accuracy=0.52.

Very strong measured medical track record across several related datasets, including araag2/PubMedQA accuracy=0.766, LangAGI-Lab/medbullets accuracy=0.562, and Voxel51/SLAKE accuracy=0.831. Its GNN score is much lower than MedGemma's, but the consistent medical-domain measurements make it a top candidate.

The GNN assigns a high predicted-performance value of 0.8820 and a strong combined score of 0.6302, but measured evidence is limited to one related medical VQA result: GoodBaiBai88/M3D-VQA accuracy=0.7995. Promising, but less certain than models with several measured medical evaluations.

This is a general QA/chat model rather than a medical specialist, but it has multiple measured QA results, led by AdaptLLM/ConvFinQA accuracy=0.7846. Performance is more modest on open-domain conversational QA datasets such as McGill-NLP/TopiOCQA accuracy=0.4996, allenai/quac accuracy=0.3973, and IBM/doc2dial accuracy=0.3933.

Its evidence is medical but mostly imaging-focused, so transfer to medical_meadow_medqa is uncertain. Still, measured medical results are strong on StanfordAIMI/chexbench accuracy=0.975 and Voxel51/SLAKE accuracy=0.781, making it a plausible lower-ranked candidate.
Medical reasoning model with o1-style chain-of-thought post-training that reports state-of-the-art MedQA accuracy among small open medical LLMs.
Llama-3.1-8B fine-tuned on the UltraMedical corpus (including USMLE/MedQA-style data); one of the top open 8B models on MedQA.
Recent 8B medical model with reasoning-style SFT targeting medical QA benchmarks like MedQA, MedMCQA, and PubMedQA.
Clinical Llama-3-8B fine-tune from M42 that has posted competitive USMLE/MedQA scores among ~8B medical models.
Aloe is a Llama-3-8B medical model trained with a mix of medical QA and instruction data, strong on MedQA-style multiple-choice questions.

Strong agreement candidate with high GNN support and consistent measured math-word-problem results: EleutherAI/asdiv accuracy=0.787, ChilleD/SVAMP accuracy=0.704, and Arietem/tabmwp accuracy=0.516. Its tool-integrated math reasoning profile is well matched to microsoft/orca-math-word-problems-200k.

It has the strongest direct SVAMP result in the evidence, with ChilleD/SVAMP accuracy=0.953, and also appears in the GNN recommendations. Its broader track record includes Joschka/big_bench_hard accuracy=0.679, supporting general reasoning ability.

This model achieved ahmedselhady/mgsm accuracy=0.792, one of the best measured results on a highly relevant GSM8K-derived multilingual grade-school math benchmark. The result is direct measured evidence on a close neighbor of the query dataset.

It is a math-specialized 7B model with strong measured performance on ahmedselhady/mgsm, reaching accuracy=0.732. MGSM is especially relevant because it is derived from grade-school math word problems similar to the query dataset.

It has the best measured result on TIGER-Lab/AIME25 with accuracy=0.82, showing strong mathematical reasoning on a challenging math QA benchmark. This is less directly grade-school-focused than SVAMP or MGSM but still strong evidence for math problem-solving capability.

On ahmedselhady/mgsm, this model achieved accuracy=0.792 on a GSM8K-derived grade-school math benchmark. Qwen3-14B variants also consistently scored 0.792 on MGSM, and unsloth/Qwen3-14B-FP8 reached accuracy=0.6698 on TIGER-Lab/AIME25.

It achieved accuracy=0.953 on ChilleD/SVAMP, an English math word-problem benchmark very close to the query format. This is the strongest measured word-problem result in the neighborhood, though it is from a small dataset.

On ahmedselhady/mgsm, this math-specialized 7B instruct model scored accuracy=0.732 on GSM8K-derived multilingual grade-school word problems. This is lower than the Qwen3-14B result but remains strong and directly aligned with the query.

It was the top model on TIGER-Lab/AIME25 with accuracy=0.82, showing strong mathematical reasoning on hard competition-style questions. Although AIME25 is less word-problem-like than MGSM or SVAMP, the high measured result suggests robust transfer potential.

It scored accuracy=0.704 on ChilleD/SVAMP, a direct English arithmetic word-problem benchmark. That measured result is competitive for the query format, even though mradermacher/ARM-7B-i1-GGUF was much higher on the same dataset at accuracy=0.953.

This has the most consistent direct math-word-problem evidence, with EleutherAI/asdiv accuracy=0.787, ChilleD/SVAMP accuracy=0.704, and Arietem/tabmwp accuracy=0.516. Its high GNN combined score of 0.7912 further supports it, but the ranking is mainly driven by the measured results on similar datasets.

It has an exceptionally strong measured result on the closely related ChilleD/SVAMP dataset with accuracy=0.953, plus solid reasoning/general QA results on Joschka/big_bench_hard accuracy=0.679 and allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.858. Although its GNN link score is tiny, the measured SVAMP result makes it a very promising fit.

This model has direct math evidence from MU-NLPC/Calc-svamp with accuracy=0.732 and harder math evidence from EleutherAI/hendrycks_math with accuracy=0.386. Its track record is narrower than ToRA or ARM, but the datasets are highly relevant to math word-problem solving.

Yi-1.5-6B-Chat shows broad reasoning competence, including HuggingFaceH4/MATH accuracy=0.405, Joschka/big_bench_hard accuracy=0.4529, and google-research-datasets/mbpp accuracy=0.709. It is less directly specialized for word problems than the top three, but its measured math and reasoning results are reasonably strong.

This is a math-specialized model and has measured STEM performance on TIGER-Lab/MMLU-STEM with accuracy=0.513. The evidence base is only one recorded evaluation, so it ranks below models with multiple directly relevant math-word-problem results.
Purpose-built math instruct model from Alibaba with state-of-the-art GSM8K/MATH performance in the 7B class; directly aligned with grade-school word-problem reasoning of Orca-Math.
14B reasoning-distilled model from DeepSeek-R1 that achieves top-tier math benchmark scores under 15B; long chain-of-thought is ideal for multi-step word problems.
NVIDIA's math-specialist instruct model trained specifically for grade-school and competition math; strong GSM8K accuracy that matches the Orca-Math problem style.
7B R1-distilled reasoning model with excellent math capability per parameter; well-suited for fine-tuning or zero-shot solving of the arithmetic word problems in this dataset.
Strong 14B general instruct model with very solid math reasoning (GSM8K ~90%); a robust non-specialist baseline that generalizes well to word-problem SFT.

Best task match: amirveyseh/acronym_identification is an English BIO-style token/span identification dataset, and this model achieved f1=0.9199. That span-extraction evidence is highly relevant to extractive keyphrase identification.
Strong measured extraction-style result on Chow05/SemEval-2014-Task-4 with f1=0.8632. Aspect term extraction with token-level tagging is a close analogue to extracting keyphrase spans.

Top GNN recommendation with combined score 0.7179, far above the other GNN candidates. Its measured track record is consistent across text QA datasets, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.762, allenai/qasc accuracy=0.685, allenai/ropes f1=0.67, and allenai/quoref f1=0.635.

Measured in the retrieved neighborhood on awinml/triviaqa with accuracy=0.776. Although QA is indirect, an 8B instruct model is plausibly useful for abstractive keyphrase generation from news articles.

Has direct news-domain evidence from heegyu/news-category-dataset with accuracy=0.7073 and f1=0.608. The task is classification rather than keyphrase extraction, but the domain match to English news articles is useful.

Most directly aligned with the query's BIO-style keyphrase extraction setup because it was evaluated on amirveyseh/acronym_identification, a token classification dataset with tokens and BIO labels, achieving f1=0.9199.

Strong measured evidence on Chow05/SemEval-2014-Task-4 with f1=0.8632, a token classification and sentiment tagging dataset involving extraction of text spans. This is task-relevant for identifying keyphrase-like spans in documents.

Has direct domain relevance because it was evaluated on heegyu/news-category-dataset, a news article dataset, with accuracy=0.7073 and f1=0.608. Although the task is classification rather than keyphrase extraction, the news-domain match is useful.

Shows solid measured NLP performance on PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification with accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7. The task is less direct than token extraction, but the result suggests strong text representation ability.

Useful as a general instruction-following model for the query's abstractive keyphrase generation side, with measured accuracy=0.776 on awinml/triviaqa. The evidence is indirect because TriviaQA is question answering rather than keyphrase generation.

The GNN gives this by far the strongest predicted fit for midas/duc2001 with combined=0.7179 and predicted-performance=0.7189. Its measured track record is also consistent across language tasks including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.762, allenai/qasc accuracy=0.685, allenai/ropes f1=0.67, and allenai/quoref f1=0.635.

This is the next strongest GNN candidate among broadly useful language models with combined=0.0092 and predicted-performance=0.4169. It has measured strength on several NLP benchmarks including allenai/sciq accuracy=0.833, aps/super_glue accuracy=0.68, and allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.5493.

Although its GNN score is low, its measured language-modeling evidence is stronger than smaller GPT-Neo variants, with EleutherAI/lambada_openai accuracy=0.6222, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.565, and Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.4273. This makes it a plausible generative fit for a DUC-style text dataset.

This model has a broader measured record than many alternatives and performs reasonably on EleutherAI/lambada_openai accuracy=0.5723 and allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.5501. It also has additional evidence on Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.3866 and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.3123, though its results are weaker than GPT-Neo-2.7B.

This is a smaller text-generation model with measured results across five datasets, including BEE-spoke-data/UltraTextbooks-2.1-fw_mix accuracy=0.5885, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.5036, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.4491. Its lower EleutherAI/lambada_openai accuracy=0.3113 and allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.176 make it a weaker but still evidence-backed option.
Strong general-purpose 14B instruct model with excellent English comprehension and instruction-following; well-suited to extract keyphrases from DUC 2001 news documents via prompting.
Newer 14B Qwen model with improved reasoning and extraction ability; expected to perform very well on keyphrase extraction from news text.
Highly capable 7B instruct model with strong IE/extraction benchmarks; a great efficient option for structured keyphrase extraction on DUC 2001.
Gemma-2 9B instruct is a top open model at its size for English understanding and instruction following, well-suited to phrase-level extraction from news.
Robust general-purpose 8B instruct model with solid English news comprehension; a reliable baseline for prompt-based keyphrase extraction on DUC 2001.

This is the closest task match: it achieved f1=0.9199 on amirveyseh/acronym_identification, a scientific-document BIO-style token/span identification dataset. That makes it highly relevant to midas/inspec keyphrase extraction.

Measured strongly on PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification with accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7, giving evidence for robust text understanding. It is less directly relevant because the evaluated task is pair classification rather than extraction.

Strong measured results on two relevant reasoning/generation benchmarks: allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.719 and RLAIF/mbpp accuracy=0.7. Its predicted-performance=0.9643 is also high, making it a credible general text model under the size cap.

Strong 7B instruction-tuned model with excellent zero/few-shot extraction capability and reliable structured output for keyphrase lists.
Smaller but highly effective seq2seq model that fine-tunes efficiently on Inspec-style keyphrase generation with competitive F1 scores.

GNN recommends it for the query and its measured track record is consistently solid across language-understanding benchmarks: Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.8279, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.7687, and allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.6288. Strongest task match: on amirveyseh/acronym_identification, a scientific-document BIO-style token classification dataset, it achieved f1=0.9199. This is the closest measured evidence to scientific keyphrase extraction.

It performed strongly on PL-MTEB/cdsce-pairclassification with accuracy=0.892 and f1=0.7. Although pair classification is indirect, the model has solid measured evidence on a text classification benchmark containing academic-style text.

It was the top model on armanc/ScienceQA, the highest-similarity evaluated neighbor, with accuracy=0.8. The task is scientific question answering rather than keyphrase extraction, so the evidence is strong but indirect.

It achieved accuracy=0.749 on armanc/ScienceQA, placing second among evaluated models on that close scientific-literature QA neighbor. This suggests useful scientific-text understanding, though not directly sequence labeling.

It achieved accuracy=1 on akshathmangudi/SciCode, and related listed variants also reached accuracy=1 on the same dataset. The scientific-domain reasoning evidence is excellent, but SciCode is less directly aligned with keyphrase extraction.

Strongest fit because it is a token-classification/span extraction model with measured f1=0.9199 on amirveyseh/acronym_identification. It also has the highest GNN combined score in the evidence, with predicted-performance=0.9528.

This is the closest measured SemEval-adjacent evidence, with f1=0.4435 on araoye01/sem_eval_2018_task_1. It also has additional NLP track record with f1=0.6521 on Abdelrahman-Rezk/Arabic_Dialect_Identification and f1=0.6162 on asas-ai/ANERCorp.

A strong general NLP fallback under the parameter limit, with measured accuracy=0.8279 on Rowan/hellaswag, accuracy=0.7687 on allenai/winogrande, and accuracy=0.6288 on allenai/ai2_arc. Its GNN predicted-performance=0.9270 is also high, though the measured tasks are less directly similar.

Relevant as a text tagging model with measured accuracy=0.679 on asas-ai/ANERCorp. The evidence is only one dataset, but the token-level Arabic NLP setting is more similar to SemEval-style language tasks than the vision models.

It has useful language-model evidence with bleu=0.558 and chrf=0.707 on Helsinki-NLP/tatoeba_mt. The task match is weaker than the higher-ranked NLP models, but its GNN predicted-performance=0.9125 suggests some potential transfer.
DeBERTa-v3-large is the strongest general-purpose encoder available in the list for token classification; well-suited for BIO keyphrase tagging after fine-tuning.
BioLinkBERT-large is pretrained on scientific/biomedical literature with citation links, giving strong domain alignment with SemEval2017 ScienceIE abstracts.
ModernBERT-large is a state-of-the-art modern encoder with long context and strong token-level representations, competitive with DeBERTa for NER-style tasks.
RoBERTa base pretrained on biomedical/scientific text — good domain match for SemEval2017 scientific abstracts even at smaller scale.
Another DeBERTa-v3-large checkpoint; strong contextual encoder that fine-tunes well for keyphrase span extraction.

Best consistency across the retrieved NER neighborhood: MultiCoNER/multiconer_v2 f1=0.921, CATIE-AQ/frenchNER_4entities f1=0.974, and Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr f1=0.9818. Although French-focused, its repeated strong token-classification results make it the most grounded candidate.

Very strong measured NER performance on two similar datasets, with MultiCoNER/multiconer_v2 f1=0.976 and Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr f1=0.99. Its limitation is that it is French-focused and trained for only three entity types, while FiNER-139 has 139 financial tags.

The strongest domain match from the GNN source: it is a financial LLM with measured results on AdaptLLM/NER f1=0.69, AdaptLLM/Headline f1=0.97, ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank accuracy=0.87 and f1=0.87, and AdaptLLM/FiQA_SA f1=0.79. Has real measured performance on a domain-specific fine-grained NER task, elenanereiss/german-ler, with f1=0.8567 and accuracy=0.9846. The legal-domain and German-language mismatch reduce confidence, but it is still grounded evidence for specialized entity extraction.

Measured well on Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr with f1=0.98, and it is in the same lineage as cmarkea/distilcamembert-base-ner. Evidence is weaker because it appears on only one similar dataset and is less directly specialized than the NER-finetuned variant.

Strongest consistency signal across three similar NER datasets: MultiCoNER/multiconer_v2 f1=0.921, CATIE-AQ/frenchNER_4entities f1=0.974, and Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr f1=0.9818. Although French rather than English financial NER, repeated high measured token-classification results make it the best-supported choice.

Very high measured NER performance on two neighboring datasets, with MultiCoNER/multiconer_v2 f1=0.976 and Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr f1=0.99. The evidence is excellent but slightly narrower because the model targets only three entity types.

Measured on a domain-specific legal NER dataset with fine-grained labels, elenanereiss/german-ler, achieving f1=0.8567 and accuracy=0.9846. This is useful evidence for specialized entity extraction, though it is German/legal rather than English/financial.

Has a strong measured NER result on Jean-Baptiste/wikiner_fr with f1=0.98. The evidence is only from one dataset and is less directly task-specialized than cmarkea/distilcamembert-base-ner, but the measured F1 is high.

Measured on the most similar neighborhood dataset Revai/earnings21, a financial earnings-call benchmark, with wer=0.0962. This is financially relevant but only indirect for FiNER-139 because the metric is ASR WER rather than NER F1.

Best match because it is a financial LLM with measured results on financial NLP, including AdaptLLM/NER f1=0.69, AdaptLLM/Headline f1=0.97, ArtGarfunkel/FinancialPhraseBank accuracy=0.87 and f1=0.87, and AdaptLLM/FiQA_SA f1=0.79.

Strong general 8B model with measured accuracy=0.797 on allenai/ai2_arc and accuracy=0.75 on HuggingFaceFW/CommonsenseQA, plus a GNN predicted-performance of 0.7624. It lacks financial NER evidence, so it ranks below the domain-specific FinMA model.

Consistent zero-shot classification record across multiple text datasets, with Yelp/yelp_review_full accuracy=0.967, google/trueteacher accuracy=0.921, alisawuffles/WANLI accuracy=0.814, and AutoIntent/massive accuracy=0.734. This broad classification evidence is useful but less directly matched to financial NER.

Has measured f1 across several classification datasets, including OxAISH-AL-LLM/wiki_toxic f1=0.787, allenai/social_bias_frames f1=0.656, PolyAI/banking77 f1=0.567, and AmazonScience/massive f1=0.518. Its zero-shot setup may transfer to label-heavy extraction, though scores are lower and less domain-specific than FinMA.

Provides a measured classifier baseline with TajaKuzmanPungersek/X-GENRE-text-genre-dataset f1=0.8 and accuracy=0.8, alongside a GNN predicted-performance of 0.8562. Evidence is limited to one non-financial genre dataset, so confidence is moderate.
DeBERTa-v3-large is a top-tier encoder for token-classification NER; this checkpoint has strong general-language priors and fine-tunes exceptionally well on domain NER like FiNER-139.
ModernBERT-large is a modern encoder with long-context support (helpful for SEC filing sentences), strong pretraining, and excellent fine-tuning behavior on token-classification tasks.
Another DeBERTa-v3-large backbone; span-oriented QA pretraining transfers well to fine-grained NER tagging over long financial numeric contexts.
Finance-domain LLM pretrained on financial corpora; domain adaptation is highly valuable for XBRL/SEC entity tagging, though decoder-only architecture is less ideal than encoders for pure NER.
DeBERTa-v3-large with strong NLI pretraining; the robust contextual representations transfer well to fine-grained financial NER labels.

Best measured result on the closest similar dataset stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.94. SNLI is highly related to MultiNLI as an English natural language inference benchmark with cosine similarity 0.8116.
Very strong measured performance on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.9238. It is an NLI-specific model evaluated on the most relevant retrieved neighbor to nyu-mll/multi_nli.

Strong measured SNLI results with accuracy=0.922 and f1=0.922 on stanfordnlp/snli. Its high performance on the closest English NLI neighbor makes it a robust candidate despite being slightly below the base variant in the evidence.

Measured accuracy=0.9165 on stanfordnlp/snli which is very close to the larger DeBERTa NLI variants. This offers strong task-specific evidence on the nearest NLI dataset while likely being more efficient.
Measured accuracy=0.9164 on stanfordnlp/snli nearly matching the small variant. It is supported by direct NLI evidence on the closest retrieved dataset and remains a promising compact option.

Very strong measured performance on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.9238. This is the second-best SNLI result and directly matches the query task type of English natural language inference.

Strong measured performance on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.922 and f1=0.922. Although slightly below the base variant on measured accuracy, it remains one of the top models on the closest NLI neighbor.

Strong measured performance on stanfordnlp/snli with accuracy=0.9164. It is nearly tied with the small variant on the closest neighbor while remaining a compact NLI-specific model.

Directly fine-tuned on MNLI plus FEVER/ANLI/LingNLI/WANLI; DeBERTa-v3-large is state-of-the-art on MNLI among sub-1B models and this checkpoint is essentially purpose-built for the task.

RoBERTa-large fine-tuned on WANLI (worker-and-AI NLI derived from MNLI); strong MNLI transfer and a solid non-DeBERTa alternative in the top tier.

Strongest direct match: on the most similar dataset Hate-speech-CNERG/hatexplain it achieved accuracy=0.8653 and f1=0.845. This is the best measured result on the closest hate-speech benchmark.

Performed well on the most similar hate-speech dataset, reaching accuracy=0.774 on Hate-speech-CNERG/hatexplain. Although only one neighboring dataset is measured, that dataset is the closest semantic match to the query.

This is directly trained for abusive, hate-speech, and offensive-content detection, matching the query domain closely. It recorded accuracy=0.698 and f1=0.687 on Hate-speech-CNERG/hatexplain.

This zero-shot classifier has broader measured evidence across text classification tasks, including f1=0.644 on allenai/social_bias_frames and f1=0.526 on AmazonScience/massive. DeBERTa-v3-large already fine-tuned for toxicity scoring, closely related to hate-speech detection and providing a strong domain-adapted starting point.
Best measured result on the highly relevant SEACrowd/xcopa causal commonsense benchmark with accuracy=0.801. This is the strongest direct evidence among the closest COPA-style datasets.

Measured on the relevant SEACrowd/xcopa benchmark with accuracy=0.6682. Its direct XCOPA evidence makes it a reasonable candidate despite being below the top two models on that dataset.

Best measured result on the highly relevant SEACrowd/xcopa causal commonsense benchmark with accuracy=0.801. This is the strongest direct evidence among the listed models for a COPA-like multiple-choice reasoning task.

Strong measured performance on SEACrowd/xcopa with accuracy=0.732 and f1=0.732. The dataset is closely aligned with Balanced COPA because it evaluates causal commonsense reasoning in a multiple-choice format.
Good measured result on SEACrowd/xcopa with accuracy=0.6682. Although below the top two, it has direct evidence on a close XCOPA-style causal reasoning benchmark.

Best measured model on the closest retrieved dataset HiTZ/XCOPA-eu with accuracy=0.628. Its evidence is directly from a COPA translation focused on cause-effect commonsense reasoning, though the score is lower than the top SEACrowd/xcopa models.

Very high measured performance on IAAR-Shanghai/VAR with accuracy=0.9729 and f1=0.9717. This evidence is less directly COPA-like than XCOPA, but it supports strong general reasoning and answer verification ability under the 14B constraint.

Has the most consistent measured QA evidence across several relevant datasets, including allenai/ai2_arc accuracy=0.762, allenai/qasc accuracy=0.685, and allenai/openbookqa accuracy=0.607. It has very strong measured objective-answer performance on IAAR-Shanghai/VAR with f1=0.9702 and accuracy=0.9714, and the GNN predicted-performance score is high at 0.8940. Evaluated on the most similar retrieved dataset, heegyu/news-category-dataset, with accuracy=0.7073 and f1=0.608 for news text classification. The domain match to professional news headlines makes this strong grounded evidence despite lower scores than the headline-cause model.

GNN-only candidate with a comparatively consistent language-benchmark track record: Rowan/hellaswag accuracy=0.699, allenai/winogrande accuracy=0.638, and PNYX/bbh accuracy=0.552. Its evidence is indirect and not news/sarcasm-specific, so it is a fallback after measured similar-dataset models.

Strongest evidence comes from a closely related headline classification task: on IlyaGusev/headline_cause it achieved accuracy=0.835. The query is also headline-based, so this measured performance on news headline understanding is highly relevant.

This model was evaluated on the most similar retrieved dataset, heegyu/news-category-dataset, with accuracy=0.7073 and f1=0.608. Its news-domain classification evidence makes it a strong fit for sarcasm news headlines.

This model has measured text-classification evidence on araoye01/sem_eval_2018_task_1 with f1=0.4435. The task is less directly matched and performance is moderate, but affect detection can still provide some transfer signal for sarcasm.

It was evaluated on SetFit/20_newsgroups with f1=0.15, which is weak but still provides measured evidence on a text-classification benchmark. The domain is less aligned than headline/news datasets, so this is a lower-confidence recommendation.

DeBERTa-v3-large is the strongest general encoder for short-text sentiment classification, and this checkpoint is already tuned on NLI/classification tasks so it fine-tunes exceptionally well on 3-class financial sentiment.
ModernBERT-large is a modern SOTA encoder with long context and strong short-text classification performance; its instruction-tuned variant transfers very well to labeled sentiment fine-tuning.
Same DeBERTa-v3-large backbone with heavy NLI pretraining, providing an excellent initialization for 3-class sentiment fine-tuning on short financial tweets.
Cardiff's Twitter-RoBERTa family is pretrained on massive Twitter corpora, giving strong in-domain priors for cashtags, hashtags, and informal financial-tweet style that a general BERT would miss.
Another Twitter-RoBERTa checkpoint already fine-tuned for tweet-level affect classification, providing a very strong warm start for financial sentiment with minimal further training.
